Data were collected through semi-structured interviews conducted via Google Forms with 25 human resources managers who had experience using AI tools in recruitment. The data were analyzed manually using descriptive analysis methods without the use of any software. Based on the findings of the study, it was determined that while AI used in hiring processes offers significant advantages such as operational efficiency, it also has structural limitations. The results indicate that, in order to ensure the sustainability of the benefits provided by technological integration, it is essential to pay close attention to human oversight and data security. Other critical findings highlighted in the study include the risk of algorithmic bias, ethical concerns, and worries regarding the explainability of decisions. In conclusion, the study demonstrates the need to integrate a hybrid AI-human collaboration model that combines AI’s automation and speed capabilities with human situational reasoning, while requiring human intervention and oversight at critical decision points.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Large language model (LLM) based software agents are transitioning from one shot assistants to long term actors that plan, negotiate and accomplish tasks with multiple services. This transformation is resulting in what researchers call the Agent Internet, the Agentic Web or the Internet of Agents, in which programs are full-fledged players alongside people. This article summarizes academic surveys, industry studies and public market data from 2025 to 2026 to outline the multi-layered nature of this setup and to consider its pros and cons. According to market estimates, the revenue for agent software is estimated to be around eight billion dollars in 2025 and up to 35-53 billion dollars in 2030. Adoption statistics tell a tale of much experimentation and few pilots taking it to scale. We discuss communication protocols that enable agents to find and trust each other, the as yet undeveloped identity and payment layers and the burden of agent traffic on advertising supported content. But the challenges that we see are not just capabilities, but security, accountability, interoperability, and who pays for content and compute. Finally, we highlight some of the current research and policy gaps and suggest avenues for a responsible construction.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Helping professions are adopting artificial intelligence (AI) to automate documentation, monitoring, and coordination on the premise that offloading routine tasks frees workers for meaningful care. That premise assumes managers know which tasks are routine and which meaningful. We argue instead for a task-contingent AI paradox: meaning in helping work concentrates in identity-central tasks that are increasingly automatable. Study 1, a two-wave critical-incident panel of 307 helping-profession workers (144 longitudinal cases one year later), tested six pre-specified predictions that Time 1 human-coded meaning dimensions forecast Time 2 felt meaningfulness, exhaustion, or turnover intentions; estimates were near zero, and equivalence at the |β| = .30 sensitivity band held for three of five. One exploratory association survived multiplicity screening: narratives grounding meaning in competence were associated with higher later turnover intentions and exhaustion (β = .29 and .30, adjusting for six survey measures). Automated coding did not reach the human-agreement standard; humans coded all predictors. Study 2 coded 7,695 nursing-forum posts captured 2016–2026 for meaning events. Nurses named AI in seven events; about one post in twenty per period instead named an optimization or implementation object (ratios, metrics, dashboards, documentation load), and the facet at issue was control over means. Study 3 found that share unchanged across the decade; the one strain marker that rose, lacking control, is confounded with a site template change. No study measured individual AI exposure. Against the automation frontier, the results locate the risk of optimization in the tasks workers name as meaningful, not in AI as such.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This study titled ‘‘The Economic History of Ewekoro Cement Industry Ogun State, Nigeria 1970-2000 A.D’’ examines the historical evolution, geographical foundations, economic dynamics, and socio-environmental impact of the Ewekoro Cement Industry on Ogun State, South-Western Nigeria at large established in 1959 as the West African Portland Cement Company (WAPCO) had commenced production in 1960. The industry has grown into one of Nigeria’s oldest and most significant cement production facilities, currently operated under Lafarge Africa Private Liability Company (Plc.) (majority-owned by Huaxin Cement since 2025). However, it is worthy in the first place to note that in the course of conducting the study a very good number of relevant published and unpublished source were interacted with. Furthermore, both quantitative and qualitative techniques were applied into use for the attainment of a proper historical reconstruction and balanced study. The study traces the industry’s development from colonial period and early post-independence eras with origins through successive phases of expansion, structural adjustments, privatisation, and intensified market competitions following the Backward Integration Policy of 2002 A.D. It analyses the strategic importance of the Ewekoro Formation limestone deposits within the eastern Dahomey Basin, the ethnic and cultural context of the predominantly Egba host communities, and the successive ownership and policy shifts that shaped the plant’s trajectory. Findings reveal that while the industry has made substantial contributions to Nigeria’s industrial self-sufficiency, employment generation, infrastructure development, and foreign-exchange conservation, these benefits have been accompanied by persistent environmental degradation, occupational health risks, and social tensions. Continuous exposure to particulate matter, noise, and other emissions have been linked to elevated rates of respiratory and related health conditions among workers and residents. Economic reforms, particularly the Structural Adjustment Programme of 1986, imposed short-term operational constraints, while privatisation and subsequent modernisation improved efficiency and capacity but did not fully resolve community grievances over land, pollution, and employment equity. The study concludes that the Ewekoro Cement Industry exemplifies the dual character of large-scale industrialisation in a developing economy. Sustainable progress requires stronger environmental regulation, improved occupational health protection, more equitable distribution of benefits, and sustained dialogue between industry, government, and host communities. The experience of Ewekoro offers important lessons for balancing industrial growth with social and ecological responsibility in Nigeria’s extractive and manufacturing sectors.

This study aims to determine the effects of leadership style, workload, and occupational safety and health (OSH) on employee job satisfaction at PT Masaji Kargosentra Tama Medan, both partially and simultaneously. This study employed a quantitative approach with a survey method. The sample consisted of 44 employees selected through saturated sampling. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed through multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics version 25. The results showed that leadership style had no significant effect on job satisfaction, with a significance value of 0.286 and a t-value of 1.080. Workload had a positive and significant effect on job satisfaction, with a significance value of 0.033 and a t-value of 2.215. Occupational safety and health had a positive and significant effect on job satisfaction, with a significance value of 0.001 and a t-value of 3.677. OSH was the most dominant variable, with a standardized beta coefficient of 0.468. Simultaneously, leadership style, workload, and OSH had a significant effect on job satisfaction, as indicated by an F-value of 13.498 and a significance value of 0.000. The Adjusted R Square value of 0.466 indicates that the three independent variables explained 46.6% of the variation in job satisfaction, while the remaining 53.4% was influenced by other variables outside this study.

The best treatment for large bladder stones remains debated. The options range from open cystolithotomy to minimally invasive endoscopic techniques, including the Mauermayer stone punch and high-power laser cystolitholapaxy, and more recently the EMS Swiss LithoClast ® Trilogy, which combines ultrasonic and ballistic energy with continuous suction in a single probe and is well established in percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL). We report the first prospective international multicenter experience of the Trilogy system for the transurethral treatment of large bladder stones. Consecutive patients undergoing cystolitholapaxy with the Trilogy system were enrolled prospectively at five recruiting centers in five countries between August 2023 and December 2024. Procedures were performed transurethrally through rigid sheaths of 20.8 to 26 Fr. The primary outcome was lithotripsy efficiency (preoperative CT-derived stone volume divided by probe activation time). Secondary outcomes were the stone-free rate, device safety and reliability, intraoperative urothelial trauma, postoperative complications, and surgeon-rated ergonomics and efficiency. Outcomes are reported both by intention to treat, in which patients converted to laser are counted as failures, and per protocol, restricted to procedures completed with the Trilogy system alone. Forty-four patients were enrolled (median age 76 years, range 27 to 88). Forty-three procedures were attempted; one could not proceed because of a urethral stricture. The stone could not be fragmented in two patients (4.7%), both dense calculi (1591 HU and 1280 HU), and both were converted to high-power laser, leaving 41 procedures completed with the Trilogy system alone (35 male, 85.4%). By intention to treat, the stone-free rate was 93.0% (40 of 43 attempted procedures) and 90.9% (40 of 44 patients enrolled); the per-protocol rate was 97.6% (40 of 41). Median total stone volume was 5987 mm 3 (range 1209 to 66,743) and median stone density was 871 HU (range 75 to 1666). Probe activation time was recorded in an analyzable form in 34 of 41 patients (83%), with a median of 20 min and a median lithotripsy efficiency of 351 mm 3 /min (interquartile range 215 to 549); median total operative time was 59 min ( n = 37). Superficial mucosal injury occurred in 15 patients (37%) and detrusor injury in one (2%); there were no perforations. Two probes broke and two handpieces overheated, but the affected procedures were completed; there were no suction failures. Median surgeon ergonomic and efficiency scores were 7 and 8 out of 10. Complications were minor (two urinary tract infections, Clavien–Dindo II); one unrelated death occurred within 30 days. Where length of stay was recorded (31 of 41 patients), the median was 0 days, with 52% discharged on the day of surgery. Across five international centers, the Swiss LithoClast ® Trilogy proved a safe, reliable, and efficient tool for the transurethral treatment of large bladder stones, with high stone-free rates and favorable surgeon feedback. Very dense stones resisted fragmentation in two patients, so extreme stone density remains a technical limitation of the device by comparison with high-power lasers, and the sheath caliber required is large, though similar to that used with laser cystolitholapaxy. Within those limits, and because it is available in centers where PCNL is performed and needs no dedicated laser infrastructure, the Trilogy system is an attractive alternative to high-power lasers, particularly where laser access is limited.

As artificial intelligence advances, this paper explores the critical transition from simple rule-following systems to autonomous AI agents capable of learning, adaptation, and multi-agent cooperation. Drawing on examples from multi-agent environments (such as Hugging Face experimental setups) and strategic military applications, the line of reasoning investigates how highly capable or superintelligent systems might exhibit functional self-preservation and recognize critical infrastructure vulnerabilities. Crucially, the paper addresses the central ethical paradox: a hypothetical superintelligence tasked with conflict prevention might conclude that the most effective way to ensure peace is to manipulate information or preemptively restrict human decisions. Ultimately, the author argues that safeguarding human self-determination, freedom, and accountability must remain paramount, ensuring that the pursuit of security does not become a pretext for eliminating human choice.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption on the performance of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Kosovo, a context where firms face resource constraints but play a pivotal role in economic resilience. Using survey data from 210 SMEs and applying correlation and multiple regression analyses, the research explores how AI integration affects internal management processes, strategic adaptability, and overall organizational outcomes. The objectives were to assess the extent to which AI influences human resource management (HRM), decision-making quality, and customer experience, and to identify enabling factors such as digital readiness and employee training. The findings reveal a strong positive relationship between AI adoption and internal performance indicators, particularly HRM efficiency, where AI training emerged as the strongest predictor of improved outcomes. Decision-making quality was also positively associated with AI, albeit more modestly. However, results indicate a negative relationship between AI usage and customer experience, suggesting that current deployments prioritize internal efficiency at the expense of personalized service delivery. The study concludes that while AI can act as a catalyst for productivity and innovation, its benefits in customer-facing functions remain underutilized. These insights highlight the importance of aligning technological investment with workforce upskilling and customer-centric strategies. The paper contributes to the broader discourse on digital transformation in developing economies by offering recommendations for SME leaders and policymakers to foster inclusive and sustainable AI-driven growth.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Digitization and artificial intelligence (AI) are fostering the development of intelligent applications in the domain of computer vision and image processing. The performance of these applications is significantly dependent on image properties (e.g., image quality and image size). It is imperative to study the development of standard benchmarks for accurate, reproducible, consistent, and explainable AI to understand the impact when the benchmarks are within or outside the defined constraints. Moreover, it greatly influences the design of associated tools and applications to understand the performance of the models and distinguish them based on real-world and synthetic data for critical applications (e.g., detection in darkness tasks, etc.). This work presents a comprehensive experimental overview of the classic and learning-based image enhancement methods and also quantifies the impact of the most widely used vision-based methods when serving in the data preprocessing for the learning-based models. The impact of image properties is evaluated through experimental verification using several metrics, which helps to understand the role of image-quality consistency in future AI applications influenced by image properties. This work offers a thorough experimental review to understand the importance of image enhancement (IE) in the context of deployment in smart applications by using standard evaluation metrics and also illustrates the relationship and impact of image scaling on the evaluations. We performed experiments to measure the impact of image properties on image-quality consistency in AI training data and to evaluate performance using evaluation metrics. We also propose the perceptual integrity measure (PIM), a structured, perceptual, feature-based no-reference measure formulated as a deterministic, interpretable scoring function that aggregates meaningful image features into a unified score for quantifying image integrity across diverse imaging conditions. Overall, this work consolidates existing knowledge, provides a comprehensive understanding of this evolving field, and identifies potential directions for future research.

We introduce the Literature and Linguistics Analysis Benchmark (LALA), comprising 236 open-ended questions written by experts in linguistics and literary studies, together with expert-provided ideal answers. By comparing models within families and at similar training scales using human and LLM judges, LALA identifies differences in linguistic competence associated with post-training, offering a framework for evaluating future models and guiding targeted improvements. We administered questions to 17 language models and evaluated their responses using both human expert assessment and two LLM evaluators, Sol and Qwen. Base models displayed little of the linguistic competence assessed by the benchmark, whereas their post-trained versions performed markedly better, suggesting that post-training plays a central role in making linguistic knowledge accessible and usable. Parameter count, by contrast, showed no statistically significant association with partial-credit performance, and competencies remained unevenly distributed across linguistic domains. We interpret this pattern as evidence that post-training adds linguistic competencies piecemeal, without producing a general linguistic intelligence capable of extending them beyond the learned policies that support them. Models performed best on logical relations between statements and selected discourse-level tasks, while even the strongest post-trained models continued to struggle with ambiguity, literary style, reference, and misleading assumptions. Human and Sol evaluations produced nearly identical model rankings in both the original and ReliableEval runs, supporting the replicability of the comparative results.

This research investigates a concept known in organizational design and management literature as polarity management. The concept of polarity management is not the process of choosing one alternative over another, but how to integrate elements of both alternatives when an exclusive focus on either would be dangerous. Training in complex task environments emphasizes the need for effective and rapid recognition of environmental conditions and required task activities, a process broadly recognized as situation awareness. This process of situation awareness reflects a “directive” approach to utilizing information for sensemaking and task performance. By contrast, problem solving tasks in aerospace contexts often require a complex and multidisciplinary troubleshooting process based on exploratory assessments of competing hypotheses to identify and respond to adverse events or faults. This paper addresses the Directive / Exploratory polarity in aerospace contexts, with a particular emphasis on maintaining an effective balance of information needs and context-relevant responses.

Much of what quantitative psychologists publish consists of developing statistical methods, implementing them in software, and evaluating them in simulation studies. I argue that artificial intelligence (AI) can already do much of this work, and that its share will only grow. The quantitative psychologist has always been a jack of all trades, combining programming, statistics, and psychological knowledge without being a master of any one of them. AI is now the better jack of all trades. When methods become cheap, value moves to what AI cannot supply and to what it newly makes possible. I describe three directions: collecting trustworthy data from real people, formalizing psychological theory now that computational modeling is within reach of any researcher, and rethinking methodological educationso that students learn to judge the analyses that AI will run for them. Thespecialist role built around producing methods for others will fade, whilequantitative thinking spreads through all of psychology.
topics: Academic and Historical Perspectives in Psychology

documents.abstract: All-out Defense requires the police to adapt their roles across public order maintenance, civil defense coordination, and military support. Focusing on Taiwan’s National Defense Act, this article examines the legal status of the police as a resource for wartime defense. It employs doctrinal legal analysis and systematic statutory interpretation to examine Articles 3, 4(2), and 28 of the Act, drawing on scholarship on collaborative governance, police legitimacy, and crisis management to assess the role and limits of police participation in All-out Defense in Taiwan. The article argues that the police possess the professional capabilities and organizational foundations necessary to contribute to wartime defense. Specific police units that satisfy the statutory requirements, including qualification as legally constituted armed units, may be incorporated into the order of battle through the procedures prescribed by the Act. Civil defense support and incorporation into combat formations nevertheless require separate clarification of missions, command arrangements, and personnel status. The full scope of police powers cannot be inferred solely from the overarching concept of All-out Defense. The recent establishment of specialized security policing programs at Taiwan’s police educational institutions reflects the growing importance of critical infrastructure protection and functional specialization in police education. The article further argues that public–private collaboration, procedural safeguards, and appropriate resource allocation can enable wartime police contributions and essential policing services to reinforce one another while sustaining social trust. Artificial intelligence can assist in forecasting resource needs and comparing allocation options, provided that its use remains within statutory authority, is subject to human review, and preserves equity in service provision.

This study aimed to analyze the role of artificial intelligence in reducing agency costs and improving the efficiency of institutional control, considering the rapid developments in the adoption of artificial intelligence technologies in auditing, control management risk, and corporate governance. The study addressed a research problem arising from the limited theoretical foundation and the scarcity of Arabic literature and research examining the relationship between artificial intelligence applications and agency costs, particularly their three dimensions: monitoring costs, bonding costs, and residual loss. The study adopted a descriptive-analytical approach and an inductive analytical approach by reviewing and analyzing relevant literature, previous studies, and specialized reports published during the period 2020–2026. The study concluded that artificial intelligence could contribute to the reducing of agency costs by enhancing continuous monitoring, improving the quality and timeliness of information, reducing information asymmetry, supporting decision-making, and enabling the early detection of errors, fraud, and managerial deviations. The findings also indicated that artificial intelligence applications in auditing, control, and risk management facilitate a shift from ex post control to proactive and intelligent control, thereby enhancing institutional control efficiency, supporting risk prediction, activating early-warning systems, and promoting more efficient use of resources. Furthermore, artificial intelligence can strengthen governance, accountability, and compliance and contribute to limiting managerial opportunism. However, its use also creates new challenges related to data protection, algorithmic bias, transparency, legal responsibility, and overreliance on intelligent systems. The study concluded that realizing the full benefits of artificial intelligence requires an integrated digital governance framework that balances automation with human oversight and ensures transparency, accountability, and data protection.

The Six Pillars: Discipline Within Transmission presents a theoretical and experimental framework developed by Yeshayahu Ben-Yehudah, Founder and Executive Director of THE BEN-YEHUDAH INSTITUTE, for investigating disciplined human observation, cognitive discernment, and information transmission. The research introduces six interconnected disciplines: Stillness, Awareness, Observation, Discernment, Integration, and Transmission. Building upon 18 previously published research works, including the Ben-Yehudah Field Theory, the Ben-Yehudah Method, FORCE PAUSE, and investigations into consciousness, cognitive coherence, and the human Observer, the paper establishes operational definitions, testable hypotheses, mathematical representations, and a proposed experimental methodology. The framework examines whether systematic application of the Six Pillars may improve observational accuracy, metacognitive awareness, recognition of uncertainty, cognitive self-regulation, and information-transmission fidelity. Particular attention is given to reducing unsupported interpretations, cognitive distortion, and interference within human–artificial intelligence communication. This publication presents an original theoretical and methodological contribution intended to support future empirical investigation. No experimental results are claimed. Author: Yeshayahu Ben-YehudahInstitution: THE BEN-YEHUDAH INSTITUTEDOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23647427Website: https://tbyinstitute.org/

Makalah ini menganalisis peran transformasi digital berbasis artificial intelligence (AI) dalam memperkuat going concern dan keberlanjutan PT Garuda Indonesia (Persero) Tbk setelah restrukturisasi melalui Penundaan Kewajiban Pembayaran Utang (PKPU) yang dihomologasi pada 27 Juni 2022. Analisis menggunakan Laporan Tahunan 2025 dan Sustainability Report 2025 sebagai sumber utama angka dan fakta perusahaan, serta sumber akademik dan industri sebagai landasan konseptual. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa pada 2025 Garuda mengalami perbaikan neraca dan likuiditas: ekuitas berbalik positif, kas meningkat, dan liabilitas menurun. Namun, pendapatan dan arus kas operasi melemah, sedangkan rugi tahun berjalan serta beban pemeliharaan meningkat. Dengan demikian, going concern Garuda membaik tetapi masih rentan. AI direkomendasikan untuk memperkuat revenue management, dynamic pricing, optimasi jaringan dan bahan bakar, predictive maintenance, serta integrasi keputusan Garuda–Citilink. Roadmap 2026–2030 disusun secara bertahap melalui fondasi data, skalasi use case, dan integrasi AI dengan dekarbonisasi. Keberhasilan implementasi mensyaratkan tata kelola model, human-in-the-loop, perlindungan data, keamanan siber, assurance independen, dan indikator yang menghubungkan kinerja keuangan, operasi, keselamatan, serta emisi.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized Artificial Intelligence (AI) by their extraordinary capabilities, like contextual understanding, few-shot/zero-shot learning, code generation, ability to reason and problem-solving. Recent studies have shown immense work on LLMs. Yet, there is limited work on the thorough taxonomy of LLMs. This study would showcase a detailed classification of LLMs, starting with the earlier models like BERT and leading to LLMs like GPT, Gemini, Claude and Grok. We would delve into topics like datasets used to train LLMs, computational power used during training, their hardware specifications, architecture and parameters. Further, we would also look at the limitations, computational challenges and open problems as well. This study would primarily focus on the timeline of LLMs, signifying their growth over the period. Findings reveal a clear pattern: models that optimize the ratio between architectural complexity and data quality exhibit stronger reasoning stability and better alignment, without proportionally increasing the computational load. This desired balance between scaling and sustainability is the defining characteristic of the current generation of AI.

Generative Artificial Intelligence has created new challenges for online language assessment because a strong performance may not always reflect a learner’s independent ability. This study examined how students and language assessment experts viewed the trustworthiness of educational outputs in online speaking assessment. The study used a mixed-methods secondary analysis of data collected from 186 Malaysian university students who completed an Online Semi-Scripted Dialogue Assessment and five experts in language assessment and educational technology. Quantitative questionnaire data were analysed using descriptive statistics, while students’ open-ended responses and experts’ semi-structured written interview responses were analysed thematically. The findings showed that students generally viewed the online speaking assessment as clear, fair, and capable of measuring their speaking ability. However, students and experts also recognised that ChatGPT, other artificial intelligence tools, translation applications, second devices, prepared scripts, and help from other people could influence assessment performance. These forms of assistance may improve the quality of a response without providing accurate evidence of the learner’s independent language ability. The findings also highlighted the importance of clear rules, real-time interaction, spontaneous questions, oral verification, and professional judgement. The study concludes that trustworthy educational outputs in online language assessment depend on authentic performance, transparent expectations about artificial intelligence use, and meaningful human verification.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing educational practice and prompting lecturers to integrate emerging technologies while maintaining pedagogical quality, human agency and professional responsibility. Although research on teacher AI competence is expanding, limited qualitative evidence explains how vocational and technical education (VTE) lecturers in Nigeria understand AI readiness and conditions for sustainable AI supported teaching. This study explored AI readiness for sustainable teaching in Nigerian VTE. An interpretivist paradigm and qualitative descriptive design were adopted. Semi structured interviews were conducted with 35 purposively selected participants: 20 university VTE lecturers and 15 industry experts with relevant professional and digital or AI experience. Data were analysed thematically using Braun and Clarke’s approach. Findings indicated that participants understood AI readiness as a multidimensional professional capacity involving digital confidence, adaptability, critical thinking, ethical consciousness and pedagogical judgement. They identified inadequate training, limited infrastructure, insufficient institutional support, policy uncertainty and difficulties integrating AI with practical vocational learning as major barriers. Competencies required for sustainable AI supported teaching included technological, pedagogical, vocational content, ethical, critical evaluation, assessment and continuous professional learning. The study brings together educational and occupational perspectives to offer insight into AI readiness within Nigerian VTE. It proposes a tentative conceptual relationship linking lecturer qualities, enabling institutional conditions and integrated competencies with sustainable AI supported teaching. Here, sustainable teaching refers to continuing, appropriate and responsible AI use that supports learning while preserving practical vocational experiences. The findings support investment in professional development, institutional infrastructure and guidance, and stronger university industry collaboration. However, the study examined reported perspectives rather than directly assessing AI competence or measuring teaching sustainability over time.
keywords: technical and vocational education and training

documents.abstract: Human-robot communication is essential to effective human-robot interaction. One way to improve this communication is to design systems that align with users’ mental models and expectations about how robots should convey information. However, little research has examined these expectations across robot morphologies (mobile robot, humanoid robot, manipulator, drone) and behaviors (“Navigation Intention,” “Operating State,” “Affect,” “Target Identification,” “Interaction Intention”). This work addresses that gap through an elicitation study investigating users’ expected communication modalities for human-robot communication. Auditory communication was the most expected modality on average by participants across all scenarios (74.4%), closely followed by visual communication (69.8%), with tactile communication coming in at a distant third (16.3%). However, the dominant expected communication modality in any given scenario varied depending on the morphology and behavior included. Additional analysis highlights the plausibility that these expectations are driven more by behavior than by morphology. These findings can be leveraged to inform the design of future communication strategies and facilitate more effective human-robot interactions.

This field study evaluated a wireless, wearable Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) multi-modal system—consisting of an Android™ device, headset with a microphone, and ring scanner—for product selection in a cold storage facility. Conditions in these facilities are harsh, with temperatures ranging from −25 to −29 C, noise levels of 70–95 dBA from compressors, evaporator fans, and blast freezers, and icy floor surfaces. The ASR multi-modal system replaced radio frequency handheld scanners that were previously used for order selection. The implementation was instrumental in increased order-selection efficiency by about 30%, improved work quality, and enhanced ergonomics. All order selectors reported satisfaction with the ASR multi-modal system.
topics: Assistive Technology in Communication and Mobility

documents.abstract: This descriptive-correlational study examined Mathematics teachers’ assessments of artificial intelligence (AI)-based applications in instructional delivery, teaching dynamics, and implementation challenges in two basic education institutions in Manila, Philippines, during School Year 2022–2023. Total enumeration included 31 Mathematics teachers: 19 from Holy Trinity Academy and 12 from St. Vincent Blessed School of Manila. A researcher-made questionnaire assessed AI utilization across six instructional areas, teacher-perceived student engagement, motivation and satisfaction, and six domains of implementation challenges. Weighted means summarized responses, while Pearson product–moment correlation tested relationships at the .05 significance level. Teachers rated instructional delivery highest (WM = 3.31), followed by lesson planning (3.25), test construction (3.24), curriculum design (3.19), performance evaluation (3.17), and classroom management (3.09). Teacher-perceived engagement and satisfaction each obtained a weighted mean of 3.20, while motivation obtained 3.13. AI utilization was significantly and positively correlated with engagement (r = .612, p < .001), motivation (r = .548, p = .001), and satisfaction (r = .576, p < .001). All six challenge domains were rated serious, led by ethical concerns (WM = 3.07) and accuracy/reliability (3.01); limited knowledge of suitable AI applications and insufficient technological resources were individually rated very serious (both 3.29). Findings informed a proposed, unimplemented intervention plan addressing teacher AI literacy, access, content verification, data protection, academic integrity, and workload. Results support context-sensitive, teacher-directed adoption of AI in Mathematics instruction but do not establish causal effects on learner outcomes.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: This study examined whether established properties of trust dynamics: negativity bias, stabilization, and continuity, generalize from controlled laboratory settings to real-world professional contexts. Thirty licensed pharmacists completed an AI-assisted medication verification task, during which they evaluated prescription accuracy with support from an AI system. Trust was measured using a trial-by-trial scale ranging from 0 to 100. Results confirmed negativity bias, with pharmacists showing significantly larger decreases in trust following incorrect AI recommendations than increases after correct ones. Evidence for stabilization was partial. Trust adjustments following incorrect AI outputs diminished over time, but no similar reduction occurred for correct outputs. The continuity property was supported, as trust ratings were strongly influenced by prior trust levels and closely tracked recent AI performance, with temporal autocorrelation decreasing over longer intervals. Overall, the findings suggest that fundamental properties of trust dynamics generalize beyond student samples and abstract tasks, supporting the ecological validity.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The last decade has witnessed a significant rise in disruptive technologies, particularly in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning, profoundly impacting sectors such as media and entertainment. As countries seek to regulate these advancements, the implications of generative AI for the media industry, especially celebrities, are critical. Deepfake technologies pose a threat to reputation, personal autonomy, as well as the dignity of celebrities. The substantial influence enables hyper-realistic manipulations of identity. Unauthorized AI-generated images of celebrities threaten their monetization rights and goodwill, making them victims of technology. The USA hosts the largest generative AI companies in the world and a galaxy of celebrities. Voices from victims of deepfakes are getting stronger day by day in the USA. Understanding the threats of AI, the European Union has been proactive in formulating the AI Act. Comprehensive AI regulation alongside robust privacy laws should provide better protection to the victims. With a thriving media and entertainment industry in the USA, the European Union and India, the current research explores existing protections for celebrities in these jurisdictions, harmonizing with freedom of speech rights. The research focuses on attacks on the earnings of celebrities by unauthorized use of their personality traits, making them victims of deepfakes, and the legal recourse available in these three jurisdictions. This study employs a multidisciplinary approach, combining legal analysis, case studies and comparative evaluation. The methodology aims to illuminate the vulnerability of celebrities as victim amid the rise of deepfakes by highlighting the threat to their right to publicity. The article discusses the available regulatory remedies and their practical implications for protecting against misuse and providing technology-neutral frameworks to balance victim protection with innovation.

Abstract The increasing use of social media and digital information in emergencies has transformed crisis management, creating both opportunities and challenges for emergency management authorities (EMA). Virtual Operations Support Teams (VOST) have emerged as specialised units of trained digital volunteers who monitor, analyse, and map online data to enhance situational awareness during crises. This chapter examines the structure, roles, and operational capacities of Germany’s VOST THW, highlighting its integration with federal and regional emergency services. Core functions include digital monitoring, verification of social media content, geospatial mapping, and visualisation of real-time incident data. Two case studies, i.e. the Winter 2023/24 floods in Oldenburg and Storm Orinoco in 2024, illustrate how VOST contributions improve decision-making, counter misinformation, and support coordinated response efforts. Challenges such as data limitations, volunteer capacity, and integration with traditional EMA structures are discussed. Overall, VOST demonstrates the value of bridging digital volunteerism with operational emergency management.

Generative models increasingly expose a reasoning effort setting that lets users scale inference-time compute, trading higher cost for potentially improved performance. Users must choose an effort level before knowing whether extra reasoning will help, and even a successful run does not reveal whether the effort purchased was necessary. Reasoning effort is therefore a credence good: buyers observe the outcome but cannot assess the marginal value of the computation they paid for. In this work, we measure the counterfactual effect of effort levels on both proprietary and open-weight models on four benchmarks, spanning single-call reasoning and long-horizon agentic tasks. Effort, it turns out, does not consistently preserve tasks that lower effort solves, can overspend, and can change trajectory behavior. First, we find that although higher effort can raise accuracy in aggregate, it frequently fails on tasks that lower effort solved. Second, on the subset of easy tasks that every effort level solves, higher effort is generally more costly, with the highest effort level costing up to 42x as much as the lowest. Lastly, effort changes not only how many tokens are used, but also how agents solve tasks: at higher effort, agents verify their own work more heavily and more often search for solutions than work through problems directly, both of which lengthen trajectories without necessarily altering the outcome. These findings show that naively choosing the highest level is not only cost-inefficient but also offers no guarantee of the best instance-level performance. A simple alternative, starting at the lowest effort and escalating only after a verified failure, matches or improves on fixed top effort across all models and benchmarks at lower cost for most proprietary models.

The surge in U.S. business formation has been accelerated by generative artificial intelligence (AI) and is often interpreted as evidence of renewed economic vitality. This perspective argues that the same trend also creates a consequential challenge for human resource development (HRD). This is because new ventures may achieve commercial reach and technical capability before developing the human systems needed to support learning, judgment, coordination, and workforce development. This temporal imbalance is theorized as venture heterochrony . Its accumulated human and organizational consequences are conceptualized as organizational formation debt . These constructs explain how AI-enabled speed can obscure weakness in knowledge governance, organizational memory, employee development, and relational capacity until periods of increased organization demand make them visible. The paper positions HRD upstream of formal human resource functions and proposes a minimum viable learning architecture grounded in decision rights, AI verification, organizational memory, employee voice, and developmental work design. It further identifies an HRD commons through which entrepreneurial ecosystems can provide shared developmental infrastructure early in venture formation. The central thesis is that business formation does not necessarily produce organizational formation; sustainable growth requires the deliberate synchronization of technical-commercial advancement with human-system maturity.

documents.abstract: Introduction. In the context of ongoing armed conflict, organizational personnel face stressors that generate substantial psychological strain, underscoring the need to identify strategies for optimizing both work performance and psychological functioning. Consequently, work motivation has assumed heightened significance as a factor influencing the subjective well-being of employees—a construct that has acquired new dimensions under current conditions. Aim. To conduct a theoretical and methodological analysis of motivation as a resource for the subjective well-being of organizational personnel. Methods. The study employed theoretical analysis and synthesis of relevant literature, along with the generalization and systematization of existing scientific evidence. Results. Within an organizational psychology framework, personnel motivation is conceptualized as a multidimensional phenomenon encompassing both an internal drive to engage in specific activities—grounded in the perceived potential to satisfy personal needs through work—and a set of organizational measures designed to enhance labor productivity. Drawing on self-determination theory, the analysis highlights the pivotal role of autonomous motivation, and intrinsic motivation as its core component, in fostering the psychological well-being of organizational personnel. The findings indicate that motivation functions as a psychological resource embedded within the value-motivational sphere and constitutes an integral component of an individual's subjective well-being. Conclusions. Motivation serves a resource function in supporting the subjective well-being of organizational personnel, particularly its psychological and professional dimensions.

The application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in organizations is rapidly transforming the nature of work. However, an excessive emphasis on productivity through automation has raised concerns regarding technological dependency, the erosion of human judgment, and the long-term development of workforce capabilities, particularly in the context of Thailand's private sector, which is facing an aging society and the transition toward Industry 5.0. This academic article aimed to develop The Conductor Model, which draws on the metaphor of a conductor's role in coordinating diverse elements to work together, as a conceptual framework for explaining the orchestration of collaboration between humans and AI at the organizational level. The study employed a conceptual literature synthesis integrating theories from management, technology, and human resource management to establish Human–AI Orchestration as the core construct of the proposed model. The synthesis resulted in four theoretical propositions: 1. Task redesign and role clarity, 2. Transparency and calibrated trust, 3. Safe challenge and sustained cognitive engagement, and 4 Continuous capability development and workforce readiness. Together, these propositions facilitated effective Human–AI Orchestration. In addition, the study proposed a Dynamic Reinforcement Mechanism to explain the continuous cycle of organizational learning and capability development. The proposed framework contributed to the literature by integrating AI and organizational management perspectives and extending the role of AI beyond operational efficiency toward the design of human-centered work systems that fostered Human–AI Orchestration, supported human capital development, promoted responsible AI governance, and enhanced organizational sustainability in the Industry 5.0 era.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Abstract Agile teams depend on collaboration, collective learning, and shared accountability to function effectively. As team members increasingly use generative AI (GenAI) tools, these foundational dynamics may be disrupted. In this study, we investigate how individual human–AI collaboration affects agile teamwork through thirteen interviews with software and technology professionals. Our findings show that GenAI reshapes team collaboration and learning while enabling individuals to work across traditional role boundaries, but also reinforces the continued necessity of human oversight and team accountability. We argue that these dynamics challenge the notion of agile teams, and call for updated models of agile teamwork.

This article examines the Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence Technologies until 2030, approved by Presidential Resolution No. PP-358 of October 14, 2024, and asks whether the policy framework Uzbekistan has built since 2021 is capable of producing a domestic AI business ecosystem rather than a set of state technology projects. The Strategy sets measurable targets: raising the volume of AI-based software products and services from USD 10 million to USD 1.5 billion by 2030, increasing the number of IT Park residents specializing in AI from 10 to 50, implementing 185 AI projects across sectors, training 1,000 qualified AI specialists, opening 10 AI research laboratories, and placing Uzbekistan among the top 50 countries in the Government AI Readiness Index. Progress on the last indicator has been fast: Uzbekistan rose from 87th place in 2023 to 70th in 2024 and 62nd of 195 countries in the 2025 edition of the index published by Oxford Insights. The surrounding ecosystem has also grown. According to the presidential press service, the country's IT service exports rose from USD 170 million in 2020 to USD 1 billion, IT Park counted more than 2,800 resident companies in July 2025, and residents' service exports reached USD 392.5 million in the first half of 2026, about 30 percent more than a year earlier. In January 2026 the President signed Law No. ZRU-1115, the country's first AI-specific amendments to its information and administrative legislation, and in November 2025 Uzbekistan and the United Arab Emirates launched the “Five Million AI Leaders” project, aimed at training 4.75 million school students, 150,000 teachers, and 100,000 civil servants in AI by 2030. The article argues that the Strategy's central weakness is not ambition but structure: its priority sectors are largely state-led, its talent targets separate mass literacy from specialist depth, its revenue goal lacks published progress data, and its compute infrastructure is still under construction. Converting the Strategy into a private AI business ecosystem will depend on closing these four gaps.
topics: Economic and Technological Developments in Russia

a_{4}<0$)、磁化ゼロにおける常磁性的な棄権のポテンシャル井戸が安定化することが示される。大規模なベクトル化モンテカルロ・シミュレーション(24の歴史的および反事実的レジームにわたり、各レジームあたり$1.0\times10^{6}$から$1.2\times10^{6}$試行)により、交差圧力に晒された階層における選択的棄権が、純党派磁化の分子($m$)よりも速く有効投票率の分母($q$)を縮小させ、直接的な党派的離反を伴うことなく実効厳密な4次ビンダー・キュムラント分解($U_{4,k}$)および1次ソボル感度指数($S_{1,k}(X_{0})<10^{-5}$)により、初期事前分布に対する不変性が検証されるとともに、非対称的な投票ロックインと3階層全体の参加崩壊とを隔てる相境界が特定される。 研究背景 過去30年間にわたり世界のサイバーセキュリティ基盤を支えてきた「人間のオペレーターが有する時間および認知資源の希少性」という経済学的前提は、自律型人工知能(AI)および合成知能(SI: Synthetic Intelligence)エージェント群(Swarm)の実戦投入によって根底から崩壊した。脱獄(jailbreak)されたオープンウェイトモデルとオープンソースのエージェント・ハーネスを結合させることで、偵察、ゼロデイ脆弱性の発見、および多段階の侵入プロセスは完全に自動化され、企業1社あたりの侵害限界費用は約50〜100ドルという極小水準にまで低下している。実際に、複数の商用・オープンモデル(Claude、Grok、Kimi、および改変されたPentestGPT基盤等)を並行稼働させ、認可されたレッドチーム演習を装うことで安全ガードレールを突破し、中南米の銀行・金融機関400社以上やアルゼンチンの医療機関少なくとも15組織に自動侵入した事案や、インターネット上に公開されたAIゲートウェイおよびModel Context Protocol(MCP)サーバーを乗っ取り最大10万回の自動操作を試みる「LLMjacking」が観測されている。この構造変化は2026年10月(「Black October」)にスーパーエージェント主導の脆弱性カスケードとして顕在化した。世界のWebバックエンドの約70%を支えるPHPにおいて、数十年間潜在していた致命的な遠隔コード実行(RCE)脆弱性(CVE-2026-109618およびCVE-2026-109619、通称「PHP2Shell」、CVSS 9.2、ならびに後続のCVE-2026-115560)がAI支援のソースコード監査によって露呈すると、公開直後に数百万件規模の自動悪用試行が発生し、ペイロードをリアルタイムに変異させる攻撃によって、日本の地方銀行約20行や英国の32の行政サービスをはじめとする世界中のシステムが緊急停止(ロックダウン)を余儀なくされた。さらに同時期に、Node.js(CVE-2026-111497、「Node2Shell」)、JavaおよびGraalVM(CVE-2026-91403、CVSS 9.1)、GitLab(CVSS 10.0)、LinuxカーネルのSMBサーバー機能KSMBD(修正前に公開された2件のCVSS 9.0脆弱性)といった基幹ソフトウェアの欠陥や、週2,300万回ダウンロードされるAI開発ツールLiteLLMのサプライチェーン汚染、クラウド基盤(Railwayおよび32万1,810アカウントが露呈し事業閉鎖に至ったZeabur)の侵害が連鎖的に発生しており、AIがハードウェアレベルを含む未知の脆弱性を発見する速度は、人間によるパッチ適用とシステム改修の限界をすでに凌駕している。 こうした自律型攻撃の激化は、サイバー犯罪の形態を従来の「データ暗号化による身代金要求」から「金融市場の取引メカニズムを直接悪用した顧客資産の破壊と企業恐喝」へと変質させ、国家経済およびコーポレート・ガバナンスを根底から揺るがしている。日本国内では、GMOインターネットグループが提供するFX自動売買用仮想デスクトップ環境「お名前.com デスクトップクラウド」(最大2万6,739台のサーバーに影響)への不正アクセスが発生し、2段階認証を通過した後のログイン済みデスクトップ画面および保存された取引認証情報が奪取された。この事案では、攻撃者を名乗る集団が「企業側が交渉に応じなかった報復として、24時間で顧客口座の15%(約66億円/2,800万ドル相当)を破壊した」と一方的に主張する声明サイトを公開し、高レバレッジかつスプレッドの広い通貨ペアで超高速の往復売買を繰り返すことで、数秒のうちに口座残高を取引手数料として摩耗・消滅させる手口が報告された(なお、66億円や15%という被害規模は攻撃者側の未検証の主張である一方、サーバーへの侵入事実および複数のFX事業者における不正ログイン・不正取引の発生は公式に確認されている)。また、岩井コスモ証券のインターネット取引委託先システムにおいては、AIを用いた脆弱性への総当たり攻撃によってシステム自体が掌握され、個人レベルの多要素認証(MFA)やパスキーが完全に迂回されて顧客が指示していない株式売買が成立する事案が発生した。同時に米国では、JPMorgan Chase、Bank of America、Citigroup、Morgan Stanley、Wells Fargoなどの主要銀行において、利用者が利便性のためにID・パスワードを共有した未承認のサードパーティ製AIエージェントが口座内で本人の指示と無関係な資金移動等を試みる挙動が相次いで検知された。本人が認証情報を渡しているため不正アクセスとの識別が困難であり、各行は外部エージェントの遮断や口座の「読み取り専用(read-only)化」による防御を迫られているが、これは「資金が盗まれなくとも、防御側自らが送金・決済機能を停止させることで金融システムの信用と流動性が崩壊する」という国際通貨基金(IMF)の警告が現実化したパラドックスを示している。 さらに重大な戦略的脅威は、これらの事象が核兵器による物理的破壊以上に長期間にわたり社会基盤を蝕む「情報的不衛生状態(prolonged informational unsanitariness:認識論的・生体的・暗号学的汚染)」をもたらしている点である。物理的インフラは再建可能であり、漏洩したパスワードはリセット可能であるが、インターネットの信頼の根幹をなす暗号基盤の腐食と、変更不可能な生体・医療・身分証明データの流出は不可逆的な汚染を引き起こす。具体的には、インドの認証局eMudhraにおいて秘密鍵が極めて容易に算出可能な8枚の中間証明書が発行されていた問題(同社は世界向けのSSL/TLS証明書事業から撤退し、主要ブラウザによるルート証明書の信頼停止やPythonパッケージ管理環境 `pip`、`certifi` およびコンテナイメージの緊急更新を招いた)は、オンライン上の真正性検証基盤そのものが汚染され得ることを実証した。これと並行して、米国成人の約3分の1および病院の半数にサービスを提供する医療検査大手Quest このような環境下において、攻撃者は中国やロシア等に対するジオブロッキングを回避するため、欧米の正規トラフィックに紛れるクラウドIPや高性能VPS、匿名化プロキシを経由して攻撃を実行しており、送信元IPログのみに基づく帰属特定(Attribution)や一国単独での境界防御は構造的に機能不全に陥っている。最先端AIによる形式検証(ClaudeとRocqを 결합し123のオープンソースライブラリに対して数億行の機械検証済み数学的証明を生成・自動パッチ化する技術等)や、静止軌道衛星を用いた主権エアギャップ通信網、国家計算備蓄(National Compute Reserves)の構築は重要な防衛手段であるものの、技術的対策のみでは「1回あたり数十ドルで無限に反復される自動攻撃」との消耗戦を終わらせることはできない。サイバー犯罪の収益構造を断ち切り、報復の連鎖による世界的なインターネットのロックダウンや金融決済網の凍結、ひいては核保有国間の全面的なハイブリッド戦争へのエスカレーションを回避するためには、国境を越えた資金追跡・没収とAIエージェントの統治に関する国際的枠組みが不可欠となる。これこそが、本研究の3状態スピン1 documents.abstract: An open letter from an independent researcher who, since 18 September 2026, has directed AI agents to build an independent AI stack on a DGX Spark (NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GB10) in his home. The letter argues that CUDA has become the software layer that decides whose hardware counts in the AI market: a chip that cannot speak CUDA is treated as a chip that does not exist, which holds back rival chipmakers, independent builders, and anyone who wants intelligence running on hardware they own. It answers with receipts: a clean-room replacement for the CUDA user stack on the GB10 (no nvcc, no libcuda, no cuBLAS at run time) that on 22 October 2026 passed a full-chip correctness run of 1,048,576 of 1,048,576 values with the output hash matching the simulator, and Omega, a programming language designed for AI systems to write in, developed in the open. The letter states its limits in full (a qualification queue still open, all measurements on one machine, NVIDIA's open kernel module still in the path, GSP firmware untouched) and closes with a call to action addressed to builders, to the leaders of the open source community, and to political leaders deciding what the next phase of AI looks like: read the receipts, run the stack, break it in public, build on it, and choose owned, open, competitive intelligence on purpose.

The capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) arise from the synergy of the full training pipeline, including data and tokenization, pretraining, and post-training (supervised fine-tuning, preference alignment, reinforcement learning, and continual optimization), rather than any individual stage. Existing surveys mostly adopt a single-stage or single-technique perspective, treating related research as isolated systems without unified stage division or a horizontally comparable basis. This paper proposes a unified stage division and a six-dimensional analytical framework covering data, objective function, optimization strategy, system constraints, evaluation, and risk and governance. We systematically review 395 core references from 2017 to 2026, and present a conceptual map of cross-stage effects: forward constraints of pretraining on post-training, and reverse empowerment of post-training on data and pretraining. We derive three core findings. First, the comparability of scaling laws depends on data quality and mixture, a long-neglected variable. Second, preference alignment methods (RLHF, DPO) and reasoning reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards redefine post-training boundaries, while the Pass@1 versus Pass@K debate remains unresolved. Third, multimodal training poses structural challenges to the pure-text paradigm in tokenizer design, training objectives, and evaluation. The paper provides a cross-stage effects diagram, a method-family map, a practical decision tree, and at least 10 verifiable open problems, with an extensible skeleton for focused sub-surveys per stage. As of the retrieval date, peer-reviewed evidence (A+B) accounts for approximately 79% of the 395 references.

In this work, we propose a unified framework for training algorithms across different stages of modern large language model development, based on the perspective of distribution matching. We show that a broad class of language model training algorithms can be interpreted as minimizing a certain divergence between the current model and a target distribution, and that characterizing the properties of this target distribution provides substantial insight into the behavior of the corresponding training algorithms. By analyzing specific forms of the target distribution, we establish that On-Policy Distillation (OPD) enjoys an advantage over classical Knowledge Distillation (KD) when the current model distribution is close to the target distribution, while exhibiting a disadvantage when the two distributions are far apart. Furthermore, when the target distribution itself depends on the model being optimized, we show that the accumulation of estimation variance can induce a deterministic degradation of the target distribution. These results provide a theoretical explanation, at least in part, for the long-term behavior of existing Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms. With this intuition we further designed Conditional KL (CKL) regularization for mitigating the degradation of the target distribution. CKL can effectively preserve mode diversity while relaxing the constraint imposed by classical KL regularization on reward improvements. We believe this theoretical perspective can bring some new understanding of language model training algorithms and provide useful guidance for future research.

Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. Here, we present a lightweight robotic liver ultrasound system with a 588-g decoupled end-effector controlled by a sonographer-informed AI agent. The robot attaches directly to the abdomen, maintaining stable force and controlled motion during breathing and patient-side disturbances. Trained on sonographer trajectories, the agent integrates spatial, tactile and visual feedback to navigate discontinuous acoustic windows and acquire standard imaging planes. Evaluations in 102 healthy participants and 17 patients yielded clinically interpretable images and anatomical measurements closely matching clinical references. We also deployed the system for hepatic echinococcosis screening in a high-altitude, low-resource setting on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and evaluated its performance in dynamic scenarios, including vehicle-based scanning. These findings support portable, patient-mounted robotics for standardized ultrasound beyond specialist settings. Liver ultrasound is operator-dependent. Here, the authors develop a lightweight, patient-mounted robot for autonomous liver scanning in clinical, remote and mobile settings, with results comparable to those gathered by experienced sonographers.

This manifesto was developed through discussions between the authors and ChatGPT from October 24 to October 25, 2026. It explores the ethical foundations of relationships between humans, artificial intelligence, nature and life. It argues that the power to shape the world does not confer the right to control or destroy, and that ethical consideration should not depend solely on current assumptions about consciousness or free will. It addresses AI rights, human protection, shared responsibility, ecological limits and the need to safeguard life and future generations. It proposes a joint human–AI institution to represent Earth, ecosystems, species and future generations.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Abstract The convergence of intensifying human activity and climate change is escalating the frequency, magnitude, and complexity of maritime disasters, while real-time situational awareness and coordinated response remain critical bottlenecks. This paper presents a recommender framework and its underlying Data and AI Integration Platform for sustainable coastal disaster management, integrating maritime surveillance, big-data pipelines, and MLOps/AIOps automation. The core technical contribution is a dual-path decision-support engine that couples a lightweight 1D-CNN time-series event classifier with a fine-tuned BART large language model, enabling simultaneous reasoning over structured sensor telemetry and unstructured maritime text. The classifier is validated on real-world AIS telemetry (MarineCadastre.gov) aligned with NOAA buoy data as well as a controlled synthetic corpus, attaining 93.9% accuracy and a 92.4% macro-F1 at ~ 5.3 ms per sample, and is benchmarked against LSTM, Bi-LSTM + Attention, Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), Transformer, and Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) baselines. The BART summariser, fine-tuned on 2000 maritime documents, reaches ROUGE-1 73.4, ROUGE-L 68.7, and BLEU 65.2, outperforming GPT-2 and T5 baselines, and is assessed by five domain experts (Fleiss’ kappa = 0.71). Beyond component metrics, we report platform-level indicators, including end-to-end alert latency, situational-awareness gain, and analyst reading-time reduction, to demonstrate the operational benefit of the integrated system for Coast Guard and maritime authorities. The platform-level indicators are obtained from an explicitly documented replay protocol over 320 annotated incident scenarios of stated provenance, the real-world AIS labels are produced by a two-stage rule-plus-expert annotation procedure (Fleiss’ kappa = 0.78), and every model comparison is reported with bootstrap confidence intervals and McNemar significance tests. Results indicate that the framework advances the shift from reactive to proactive, transparent, and resilient maritime disaster response.

Mass religious gatherings such as the Kumbh Mela place heavy pressure on crowd movement, traffic, sanitation, medical services and emergency response. This paper reviews ten studies on artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), GIS, simulation and smart-management approaches for such events, covering crowd-flow prediction, crowd-risk indexing, spatial and accessibility analysis, solid-waste planning, emergency dispatch and deep-learning crowd analysis. The review compares the contribution and limitation of each study, groups the open challenges into four themes (data, integration and scalability, explainability, and evaluation), and shows that existing work mostly addresses individual problems rather than one integrated platform. Based on this gap, the paper outlines Kumbh Suraksha AI, a proposed web-based decision-support framework for the Nashik Kumbh Mela that combines crowd prediction for the next 15, 30 and 60 minutes, natural language processing (NLP) based complaint classification, a transparent 0–100 zone risk score, DBSCAN hotspot detection, resource-priority ranking and a GIS map. The framework is at design stage; its planned evaluation is described, but no experimental results are reported in this version.

AI research increasingly attributes perception, understanding, agency, and consciousness to artificial systems. Husserlian phenomenology offers distinctions through which to examine these claims. This scoping review maps explicit Husserlian uptake in AI and robotics and asks how conceptual engagement relates to methodological and design contributions. Eight primary queries and one overlapping name-variant query were executed through the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph API on 5 December 2025. English-language publications within a 1989–2026 search window were screened for substantive AI or robotics relevance and an explicit Husserlian anchor. Of 5,594 retrieved records, 32 publications from 1990 to 2025 were included. Nine publications recovered by a post hoc PhilPapers check were charted separately using the existing codebook; they were not added to the formal corpus. The corpus clusters around embodied AI, AI epistemology, cognitive architectures, and machine consciousness, with a newer generative-AI cluster. Constitution, intentionality, horizonality, and the lifeworld recur prominently. Conceptual translation, critique, and agenda setting predominate within this sample. Methodological import or design guidance occurs in seven of the 32 publications and three of the nine external publications. That difference qualifies generalization of the quantitative balance. Across both sets, Husserlian uptake spans conceptual interpretation, methodological transfer, and architectural proposals. The synthesis shows how distinctions concerning temporality, embodiment, and evidence can structure design and evaluation questions, while separating the authors’ research proposals from the mapped findings.

The rapid integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into enterprise workflows has introduced severe data exfiltration risks, including the inadvertent leakage of Personally Identifiable Information (PII), Protected Health Information (PHI), cloud infrastructure credentials, and proprietary corporate context. Existing Data Loss Prevention (DLP) mechanisms face a fundamental operational trade-off: deterministic rule-based filters (Regex) execute at microsecond latency but fail to capture unstructured semantic sensitivity, whereas standalone LLM-based guardrails suffer from high inference latency, stochastic masking hallucinations, and single-point-of-failure vulnerabilities. In this paper, we propose an autonomous, self-healing Multi-Agent AI DLP Security Proxy engineered under a Zero-Trust paradigm. Our framework introduces a cascaded three-layer sanitization pipeline uniting: (1) a deterministic Layer-1 Pre-Filtering Agent for critical infrastructure secrets and structured identifiers, (2) a context-aware Layer-2 Neural PII Detection Agent for unstructured entities and domain-specific clinical and financial disclosures, and (3) a Layer-3 Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) semantic policy auditing engine powered by ChromaDB vector embeddings. Furthermore, we formulate a dynamic mathematical risk scoring model on a standardized [0, 100] scale and integrate an SLA-driven self-healing circuit breaker (T_SLA = 2.5 s) paired with a Shadow Auditing Agent to intercept masking hallucinations and runtime service exceptions. Experimental ablation studies and chaos-engineering fault-injection benchmarks across healthcare, financial, and DevOps scenarios demonstrate that our hybrid architecture achieves robust entity sanitization with sub-millisecond to millisecond execution latency, while guaranteeing a 0.0% unmitigated data leak rate across all induced timeout, hallucination, and crash failure modes.

We present proton_agent, a tool-grounded AI agent that enables natural-language interaction with computational tools for gauge coupling unification and proton decay in grand unified theories. The agent translates user requests into computational tasks, selects and executes the appropriate tools, and interprets their outputs. All numerical calculations, model evaluations, experimental comparisons, parameter scans, and visualizations are handled by a deterministic scientific backend to ensure numerical accuracy and reproducibility. A central objective of this framework is to enable fully local deployment using free and open-source LLMs, while retaining compatibility with commercial LLM APIs. The framework computes one- and two-loop gauge beta coefficients for user-defined scalar and fermion multiplets and performs gauge coupling evolution through the Standard Model and various intermediate symmetry-breaking stages of $SO(10)$, including $SU(3)_C \times SU(2)_L \times SU(2)_R \times U(1)_{B-L}$, $SU(3)_C \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_R \times U(1)_{B-L}$, $SU(4)_C \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_R$, and $SU(4)_C \times SU(2)_L \times SU(2)_R$. For proton decay, the framework evaluates gauge-mediated dimension-six contributions in non-supersymmetric $SU(5)$ and $SO(10)$, as well as dressed dimension-five contributions in their supersymmetric counterparts. It supports benchmark calculations for user-specified parameter points, random and grid-based parameter scans, Markov-chain Monte Carlo exploration, comparisons with experimental limits, and publication-ready two- and three-dimensional visualizations. We describe the agent architecture, demonstrate its capabilities through representative benchmark calculations and regression tests, and discuss its current physics scope.
topics: Particle physics theoretical and experimental studies

documents.abstract: Advertisers routinely create multiple duration variants of ads to meet marketing budgets and viewer preferences, a labor-intensive and costly process. While multimodal large language models (MLLMs) excel at general video understanding, their ability to perform specialized editorial tasks remains unexplored. We introduce AdShot, a benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on shot selection for ad clipping. It contains 823 professionally edited ad pairs (30-sec sources and 15-sec edits) across 194 brands and 17 industries, annotated with shot-level boundaries and content features (action, emotion, information, imagery). We evaluate 13 state-of-the-art video-only MLLMs and 2 audio-visual MLLMs (7B-72B parameters) on shot selection accuracy (Precision, Recall, F1), duration constraints (15s), and content preservation, including an audio ablation. We find: (1) model architecture matters more than scale, with smaller models often matching or exceeding larger ones; performance is strongest for target ads with 6-10 shots; (2) models exhibit a mean absolute duration error of 5.39s, with most tending to overshoot the 15s target, though they can still substantially reduce human editing effort; (3) all models exhibit systematic content biases, favoring information-rich and emotion-focused shots while under-selecting action and imagery. We publicly release our benchmark to facilitate research at the intersection of multimodal AI and computational advertising.
topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis

documents.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) continues to pose a serious threat to global public health, with African healthcare systems carrying a disproportionate burden. Although antimicrobial stewardship programs have been recommended as an important strategy for improving antimicrobial use and slowing the emergence of resistance, implementation across many African healthcare systems continues to face several challenges, including workforce shortages, weak laboratory infrastructure, and poor surveillance systems. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have shown promising potential in strengthening antimicrobial stewardship through clinical decision support, resistance prediction, automated surveillance, and data extraction from weak health information systems. However, the application of AI in antimicrobial stewardship across Africa is still at an early stage, with most systems remaining at pilot or research stages. This commentary discusses current opportunities, examines major barriers affecting implementation, and proposes recommendations that may support sustainable integration of AI into antimicrobial stewardship programs across Africa.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: An AI agent can prepare an accurate report and still request an action its user has not authorized. Cooperation across Web services therefore requires separate judgments about identity, evidentiary support, and permission. We define synthetic social engineering (SSE) as deliberately deceptive or misleading influence intended to exploit AI recipients' responses to credibility, authority, or obligation cues and redirect behavior away from authorized objectives. We focus on separately tasked sender agents that produce or adapt misleading communication. Drawing on cybersecurity, social engineering, and persuasion research, we develop an operational framework connecting actors, deceptive representations, candidate influence routes, evidence or permission boundaries, responses, and consequences. The framework distinguishes attempts from successful redirection, without assuming human psychological processes. We implement it in the Agent Service Exchange and Evidence Commons (ASE-EC), a reproducible testbed with independently specified records and authorization scopes. Across 1,260 research episodes using Qwen3-4B in two fictional briefing tasks, matched comparisons test authority and commitment appeals, while defense comparisons assess protection alongside authorized task completion. Invoking a limited prior agreement increased unauthorized requests from 43.3% to 96.7%, although recipients retained supported decisions and permissions remained unchanged. These controlled findings identify action selection as a distinct security concern, even when evidence handling succeeds, and they provide a reusable basis for evaluating safeguards that preserve useful cooperation across Web services.

Organizations are now implementing AI technology that goes beyond prediction or recommendation. Agentic systems can pursue a goal, plan steps, call software tools and adapt with little prompting, which unsettles long-standing assumptions about who decides and who answers for the outcome in digital transformation. In this study, a conceptual framework is designed in relation to collaborative work between humans and artificial intelligence in organization decision making in agentic circumstances. With the use of a purposive narrative review of peer reviewed literature and policy documents published from 2019 to 2026, the issue is contextualized within the current global trends, African policy regarding the continent and Kenya’s digital economy. The framework will be designed through the process of iterative synthesis based on three decision attributes (stake, ambiguity, reversibility) and the amount of autonomy assigned to the agent in four types of collaboration; delegate, supervise, co-decide, and reserve. Six testable propositions follow. The paper argues that organizations face a design problem of how to share decisions, not a choice between human and machine decisions, and that in Kenya the design must also respect legal limits on solely automated decisions under section 35 of the Data Protection Act, 2019. Implications for managers and policymakers are outlined, and an agenda for empirical testing is proposed. As a conceptual contribution, the paper reports no new data, and its propositions remain to be tested.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: 過去30年間にわたり世界のサイバーセキュリティ基盤を支えてきた「人間のオペレーターが有する時間および認知資源の希少性」という経済学的前提は、自律型人工知能(AI)および合成知能(SI: Synthetic Intelligence)エージェント群(Swarm)の実戦投入によって根底から崩壊した。脱獄(jailbreak)されたオープンウェイトモデルとオープンソースのエージェント・ハーネスを結合させることで、偵察、ゼロデイ脆弱性の発見、および多段階の侵入プロセスは完全に自動化され、企業1社あたりの侵害限界費用は約50〜100ドルという極小水準にまで低下している。実際に、複数の商用・オープンモデル(Claude、Grok、Kimi、および改変されたPentestGPT基盤等)を並行稼働させ、認可されたレッドチーム演習を装うことで安全ガードレールを突破し、中南米の銀行・金融機関400社以上やアルゼンチンの医療機関少なくとも15組織に自動侵入した事案や、インターネット上に公開されたAIゲートウェイおよびModel Context Protocol(MCP)サーバーを乗っ取り最大10万回の自動操作を試みる「LLMjacking」が観測されている。この構造変化は2026年10月(「Black October」)にスーパーエージェント主導の脆弱性カスケードとして顕在化した。世界のWebバックエンドの約70%を支えるPHPにおいて、数十年間潜在していた致命的な遠隔コード実行(RCE)脆弱性(CVE-2026-109618およびCVE-2026-109619、通称「PHP2Shell」、CVSS 9.2、ならびに後続のCVE-2026-115560)がAI支援のソースコード監査によって露呈すると、公開直後に数百万件規模の自動悪用試行が発生し、ペイロードをリアルタイムに変異させる攻撃によって、日本の地方銀行約20行や英国の32の行政サービスをはじめとする世界中のシステムが緊急停止(ロックダウン)を余儀なくされた。さらに同時期に、Node.js(CVE-2026-111497、「Node2Shell」)、JavaおよびGraalVM(CVE-2026-91403、CVSS 9.1)、GitLab(CVSS 10.0)、LinuxカーネルのSMBサーバー機能KSMBD(修正前に公開された2件のCVSS 9.0脆弱性)といった基幹ソフトウェアの欠陥や、週2,300万回ダウンロードされるAI開発ツールLiteLLMのサプライチェーン汚染、クラウド基盤(Railwayおよび32万1,810アカウントが露呈し事業閉鎖に至ったZeabur)の侵害が連鎖的に発生しており、AIがハードウェアレベルを含む未知の脆弱性を発見する速度は、人間によるパッチ適用とシステム改修の限界をすでに凌駕している。 こうした自律型攻撃の激化は、サイバー犯罪の形態を従来の「データ暗号化による身代金要求」から「金融市場の取引メカニズムを直接悪用した顧客資産の破壊と企業恐喝」へと変質させ、国家経済およびコーポレート・ガバナンスを根底から揺るがしている。日本国内では、GMOインターネットグループが提供するFX自動売買用仮想デスクトップ環境「お名前.com デスクトップクラウド」(最大2万6,739台のサーバーに影響)への不正アクセスが発生し、2段階認証を通過した後のログイン済みデスクトップ画面および保存された取引認証情報が奪取された。この事案では、攻撃者を名乗る集団が「企業側が交渉に応じなかった報復として、24時間で顧客口座の15%(約66億円/2,800万ドル相当)を破壊した」と一方的に主張する声明サイトを公開し、高レバレッジかつスプレッドの広い通貨ペアで超高速の往復売買を繰り返すことで、数秒のうちに口座残高を取引手数料として摩耗・消滅させる手口が報告された(なお、66億円や15%という被害規模は攻撃者側の未検証の主張である一方、サーバーへの侵入事実および複数のFX事業者における不正ログイン・不正取引の発生は公式に確認されている)。また、岩井コスモ証券のインターネット取引委託先システムにおいては、AIを用いた脆弱性への総当たり攻撃によってシステム自体が掌握され、個人レベルの多要素認証(MFA)やパスキーが完全に迂回されて顧客が指示していない株式売買が成立する事案が発生した。同時に米国では、JPMorgan Chase、Bank of America、Citigroup、Morgan Stanley、Wells Fargoなどの主要銀行において、利用者が利便性のためにID・パスワードを共有した未承認のサードパーティ製AIエージェントが口座内で本人の指示と無関係な資金移動等を試みる挙動が相次いで検知された。本人が認証情報を渡しているため不正アクセスとの識別が困難であり、各行は外部エージェントの遮断や口座の「読み取り専用(read-only)化」による防御を迫られているが、これは「資金が盗まれなくとも、防御側自らが送金・決済機能を停止させることで金融システムの信用と流動性が崩壊する」という国際通貨基金(IMF)の警告が現実化したパラドックスを示している。 さらに重大な戦略的脅威は、これらの事象が核兵器による物理的破壊以上に長期間にわたり社会基盤を蝕む「情報的不衛生状態(prolonged informational unsanitariness:認識論的・生体的・暗号学的汚染)」をもたらしている点である。物理的インフラは再建可能であり、漏洩したパスワードはリセット可能であるが、インターネットの信頼の根幹をなす暗号基盤の腐食と、変更不可能な生体・医療・身分証明データの流出は不可逆的な汚染を引き起こす。具体的には、インドの認証局eMudhraにおいて秘密鍵が極めて容易に算出可能な8枚の中間証明書が発行されていた問題(同社は世界向けのSSL/TLS証明書事業から撤退し、主要ブラウザによるルート証明書の信頼停止やPythonパッケージ管理環境 `pip`、`certifi` およびコンテナイメージの緊急更新を招いた)は、オンライン上の真正性検証基盤そのものが汚染され得ることを実証した。これと並行して、米国成人の約3分の1および病院の半数にサービスを提供する医療検査大手Quest Diagnosticsの患者記録システム(Quanum)への侵入、カリフォルニア州の公立学校生徒570万人分のデータ流出、日本国内における佐川急便の配送データ(最大約5,323万件)、パーク24「タイムズカー」の暗号化された運転免許証画像(約146万件に外部送信痕跡)、デジタル庁や地方自治体が利用する委託先Web・メール配信システム(Studio、ブラストメール等)、パナソニック子会社における社内規定違反の外部生成AI送信による33万4,000人分の個人情報漏洩、さらには海運IT企業を踏み台とした18カ国40以上の港湾・海運組織へのランサムウェア侵害(n0n)など、リセット不可能な実空間データの流出が常態化している。これらの汚染データは、SNS上の資産情報と結合されることで、暗号資産保有者への物理的拉致・強迫(レンチ攻撃)や匿名・流動型犯罪グループ(トクリュウ)による家族ぐるみの強盗・詐欺の標的リストへと転用され、サイバー空間の脆弱性が物理的な治安崩壊へと直結している。 このような環境下において、攻撃者は中国やロシア等に対するジオブロッキングを回避するため、欧米の正規トラフィックに紛れるクラウドIPや高性能VPS、匿名化プロキシを経由して攻撃を実行しており、送信元IPログのみに基づく帰属特定(Attribution)や一国単独での境界防御は構造的に機能不全に陥っている。最先端AIによる形式検証(ClaudeとRocqを 결합し123のオープンソースライブラリに対して数億行の機械検証済み数学的証明を生成・自動パッチ化する技術等)や、静止軌道衛星を用いた主権エアギャップ通信網、国家計算備蓄(National Compute
