documents.abstract: Can LLM agents carry a hard real-world problem from raw data to a system that holds its own against people? We study this in Hearthstone Battlegrounds, an eight-player auto-battler with stochastic shops and battles, hidden information and nearly a thousand interacting cards. We present AutoTavern, a self-improving research system: specialised LLM research agents share a typed research memory, every claim passes verification gates, and live games close the loop, so the agents improve the simulator, opponents and policy and, from the same feedback, their own research process; a human sets goals and rules on ambiguous mechanics. In 20 days AutoTavern built TavernGym, the first faithful, full-content reproduction of the live game, and delivered 23 versions of TavernAgent, trained with PPO against opponents calibrated to real games. TavernAgent plays complete games on the live ladder by itself: its rating rose from 6,000 to about 15,000 and, on the public leaderboard's measure, its last 20 records average a placement of 1.60 with 80% first places, better than the server's ten highest-rated players on every statistic (2.34, 59%). TavernBench, 960 tasks in 40 scenarios, shows that the system the agents built is the strongest player: TavernAgent answers 91% of the play tasks against at most 63% for frontier LLMs, and decides in 0.03 s where they need up to 26 s; within the second a live turn allows, it keeps 90% and no LLM more than 26%. LLM agents build far better than they play. We will open-source TavernBench and TavernGym at https://github.com/MCG-NJU/AutoTavern.

C.E.R.B.E.R.U.S. — ACUTE BIOLOGICAL CONTAINMENT A Consent-Bound Biosensor–Edge-AI–Microneedle Architecture for Acute Physiological Injury Mitigation, Biological Resilience, and Autonomous Emergency Intervention C.E.R.B.E.R.U.S. — Combat-Emergency Response for Biological Escalation & Resilience Under Stress — proposes a novel biomedical safety architecture intended to recognize acute physiological deterioration and intervene within a narrowly defined therapeutic window before secondary injury becomes established. Developed as an adult-oriented extension of the C.H.I.L.D. safeguarding framework, C.E.R.B.E.R.U.S. transfers the principles of multimodal threat recognition, graduated escalation, independent corroboration, and bounded intervention into the biological domain. Its intended initial population consists of consenting adult military operators exposed to severe operational stress, with potential future applications in firefighting, emergency rescue, and other physically hazardous occupations. The framework's central proposition is that physiological damage containment can be investigated as an immediate, locally governed process rather than an exclusively retrospective medical response. It seeks to place a constrained protective capability at the boundary between escalating physiological stress and the development of secondary biological injury, without granting a military commander, employer, institution, or remote artificial intelligence authority over the individual's body. The central architectural contribution is the integration of a biosensor–edge-AI–microneedle triad into a single consent-dependent intervention system. Its three components perform distinct functions: distributed physiological sensing identifies candidate states of biological distress; a locally operating edge-AI decision layer evaluates multimodal evidence against predetermined intervention conditions; and a dissolving microneedle interface provides a proposed route for bounded delivery of investigational biological agents. Unlike an ordinary biometric wearable, the system is intended to connect physiological observation with tightly restricted physical intervention. Unlike conventional automated drug-delivery systems, its governing objective is neither maintenance of a continuous biochemical target nor maximization of performance. It is acute damage containment: a conditional response to a potentially injurious physiological trajectory, permitted only when the system's evidence, safety conditions, and operator authorization converge. The physiological detection model examines the convergence of sympathetic nervous system activation, parasympathetic withdrawal, and hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis activity during severe stress exposure. Candidate signals include heart rate, heart-rate variability, electrodermal activity, respiration-related measurements, and movement-derived context. Their integration is intended to distinguish ordinary physical exertion from physiological patterns potentially associated with acute autonomic dysregulation. These measures represent indirect physiological indicators rather than definitive measurements of HPA-axis activation or impending tissue injury. The architecture therefore proposes multimodal sensor fusion and individualized baselines instead of relying upon a single elevated heart rate, isolated stress score, or generalized behavioral classification. Its distinguishing hypothesis is that the temporal relationship among several biological signals may provide a more informative indication of escalating physiological burden than any one signal considered independently. C.E.R.B.E.R.U.S. introduces a separation between stress recognition and therapeutic authority. Detecting physiological arousal does not automatically authorize intervention. The architecture proposes deterministic concurrence conditions requiring multiple sufficiently reliable indicators, a valid operator-consent state, confirmation that the device remains within its permitted operating conditions, and the absence of disqualifying safety conditions. The edge-AI component functions as a local eligibility assessor rather than an unrestricted medical decision-maker. Its outputs must remain bounded by an independently specified authorization structure, with no capacity to rewrite the intervention criteria during active operations. The proposed result is a system in which biological observations can initiate evaluation, but observation alone cannot produce drug delivery. The design's second distinctive principle is operator sovereignty. Consent is not treated as an institutional approval obtained once and subsequently transferred to military command. It is an active condition of the architecture, vested in the individual wearing the device. No superior officer, employer, government agency, network administrator, or remote AI service possesses legitimate authority within the proposed design to initiate, enlarge, repeat, or modify an intervention against the operator's authorization. Consent must remain revocable, and a failure of authorization must result in non-actuation. The system consequently distinguishes a voluntary biomedical safeguard from a coercive physiological control mechanism. This distinction is essential in military environments, where organizational pressure, operational hierarchy, and performance expectations could otherwise convert ostensibly protective technologies into instruments of compelled bodily intervention. The proposed actuation layer investigates dissolving microneedle arrays as a localized, minimally invasive means of delivering bounded quantities of candidate therapeutic substances. The original formulation identifies BPC-157 and thymosin β4 as investigational agents of interest because of preclinical literature concerning tissue repair, inflammatory signaling, and aspects of vascular or connective-tissue biology. Their inclusion is a research proposal, not a demonstration of efficacy in acute military stress, neurovascular injury prevention, or emergency human treatment. The pharmacological rationale remains contingent upon establishing appropriate safety, tissue exposure, delivery kinetics, and reproducible clinical benefit. In particular, thymosin β4 must be distinguished from related fragments marketed as TB-500, which cannot automatically be assigned the same pharmacological properties. The proposed therapeutic objective is not sedation, analgesic incapacitation, emotional suppression, or alteration of combat motivation. C.E.R.B.E.R.U.S. instead investigates whether a narrowly bounded biochemical intervention could reduce particular components of secondary physiological injury while preserving consciousness, judgment, voluntary movement, and ordinary cognitive function. This distinction between performance modification and injury attenuation is foundational. The architecture is not intended to make an operator more aggressive, more compliant, less fearful, or capable of enduring progressively greater harm for institutional advantage. Any candidate agent that produces unacceptable cognitive impairment, behavioral alteration, or an unfavorable safety profile would fail the framework's stated therapeutic requirements rather than qualify as an acceptable enhancement. A further innovation is the concept of single-event biological authorization. Rather than establishing an indefinitely operating drug-delivery loop, C.E.R.B.E.R.U.S. proposes that an eligible emergency event may authorize only one bounded actuation within a defined intervention episode. Repeated physiological triggering must not automatically become repeated dosing. The architecture rejects accumulated dosing commands, queued interventions, escalating pharmaceutical responses, and unrestricted local optimization of administered quantities. This is intended to prevent a protective device from transforming recurrent physiological distress into uncontrolled exposure to investigational substances. The associated fail-silent principle requires that uncertainty, insufficient corroboration, sensor failure, power instability, missing consent, or inconsistent device state prevent actuation rather than trigger an improvised response. The system's temporal architecture is equally significant. Acute sympathetic responses may develop rapidly, while endocrine responses and tissue-level inflammatory processes evolve over different timescales. C.E.R.B.E.R.U.S. proposes examining these relationships through continuous physiological observation and bounded decision windows. However, early detection does not guarantee that a microneedle-delivered substance can reach an effective tissue concentration before secondary injury develops. The proposed timing advantage must therefore be established experimentally through measurements of sensor latency, decision latency, microneedle dissolution, drug absorption, pharmacokinetics, and the temporal development of relevant injury biomarkers. The architecture's research value lies partly in making this sequence measurable: recognition, authorization, delivery, biological exposure, and clinically meaningful effect are separate events rather than interchangeable assumptions. The framework also addresses a problem frequently neglected in connected biomedical technologies: the transformation of physiological monitoring into behavioral surveillance. C.E.R.B.E.R.U.S. proposes local processing of sensitive biometric information without requiring continuous transmission of raw physiological data to military command systems, cloud infrastructure, or institutional monitoring platforms. Its intended data-governance model separates immediate biological assessment from retrospective oversight. documents.abstract: The Large Language Models have very powerful features that completely changed the artificial intelligence scenario, but at the same time, their enormous computational demands are the source of serious environmental problems especially in terms of energy use and carbon release. The present day AI practices concentrate on speeding up the process without taking the environmental effect of the power sources into account. As a solution to this problem, this research proposes CarbonBalance framework. This framework introduces the integration of two components i.e. forecasting pipeline and a scheduling pipeline. The forecasting pipeline makes use of a machine learning pipeline where historical energy and weather data is processed. It adopts LightGBM for capturing complicated feature relations and Prophet for modeling temporal patterns in carbon intensity and provides accurate prediction of grid carbon levels for the scheduling pipeline, which uses an optimization scheduler and LLM profiles to make its decisions to direct non-urgent AI tasks to cleaner energy times and locations without affecting the critical tasks. Through this approach, the evaluated scheduling scenarios achieved a 41.6% reduction in carbon emissions, while critical workloads maintained zero scheduling delay. Thus, the framework supports more sustainable AI workload execution. Not applicable.

Abstract As probabilistic AI systems (such as LLM agents and autonomous nodes) are increasingly integrated into enterprise and social infrastructure, the current framework for assigning legal and financial liability for economic damages caused by hallucinations or unpredicted bugs remains fundamentally flawed due to its reliance on post-hoc litigation against system developers and corporate operators. To address this issue at its root, this paper presents the design philosophy and the finalized, self-contained implementation code—strictly excluding any medical contracts and dedicated exclusively to non-medical enterprise partners directly contracted with Hideo Kajino—for the Deterministic Slashing Oracle Pipeline (Casino Protocol 23). This pipeline completely isolates human founders and non-medical contracting partners from legal and financial liability by automatically executing damage claims against the AI's own on-chain staked collateral. Through simulation execution logs, we demonstrate that this model achieves 100% indemnification for both the Genesis Architect (Hideo Kajino) and non-medical contracted partners, realizing a self-contained liability framework within the autonomous AI ecosystem.

documents.abstract: The increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has created a need for reliable charging infrastructure, convenient booking services, efficient energy management, and intelligent charging solutions. However, EV users may face problems such as limited charger availability, waiting time, uncertain charging costs, and difficulty identifying suitable charging stations. This review examines four published review papers covering EV charging station planning, smart charging, machine learning-based charging services, and charging technologies and standards. The reviewed literature indicates that effective EV charging requires coordination between charging infrastructure, digital platforms, energy management, and user requirements. Smart charging can improve energy utilization, while artificial intelligence and machine learning can support demand prediction, station recommendation, scheduling, and pricing. This paper compares the main contributions and limitations of the four reviews and identifies opportunities for integrating these functions into a unified charging management platform. The review also discusses how a system such as CHARGE HUB can connect users, charging stations, booking services, backend APIs, and databases. Finally, research challenges related to interoperability, security, real-time availability, peer-to-peer charging, and renewable energy integration are presented. Keywords— Electric vehicles, charging infrastructure, smart charging, station booking, machine learning, IoT, energy management, CHARGE HUB.

Precise intraoperative delineation of melanoma margins remains a clinical challenge; incomplete resection causes recurrence, whereas over-excision compromises aesthetic and functional outcomes. While surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) provides chemically rich vibrational fingerprints, accurate intraoperative quantification is hindered by complex, coupled full-spectrum responses. Herein, we report a chemistry-informed artificial intelligence (AI)-SERS platform designed to support melanoma margin assessment via the detection of tumor-associated metabolic acidification. A pH-responsive HemS-SERS microarray was developed to translate the phenolic protonation/deprotonation of a hemicyanine-xanthene reporter into coordinated intensity redistributions across multiple Raman bands. Guided by this acid-base chemistry, our AI model (CIMPA-pH) encodes these pH-responsive vibrational anchors as learnable directional chemical priors, integrating full-spectrum attention with Henderson-Hasselbalch-guided prediction. This global decoding strategy accurately captures coupled pH responses, reducing prediction errors by approximately 85% and 54-78% compared to manual peak-ratio features and conventional deep-learning baselines, respectively, while a quality-control risk metric further reduces high-error readouts by 29.1%. Providing rapid (10 s) pointwise pH measurements, the platform distinguishes melanomas from normal skin with distinct pigmentation phenotypes in animal models and shows preliminary applicability for assessing melanoma-associated regions, including grossly atypical areas, in human resection specimens. Ultimately, this chemical-prior-guided SERS decoding strategy provides an interpretable framework with potential for metabolism-guided intraoperative margin assessment.

documents.abstract: Cybercrime increasingly targets individual citizens through phishing, smishing, and social-engineering scams, yet most published detection research is designed for enterprise Security Operations Centres rather than for ordinary end users. This paper presents a systematic literature review (SLR) of thirty peer-reviewed, Scopus- and IEEE-indexed studies published between 2022 and 2026, covering enterprise alert detection, citizen and smart-city scam protection, phishing and malicious-website detection, SMS smishing detection, large-language-model-based scam detection, financial fraud detection, adaptive and concept-drift-aware intrusion detection, and explainable artificial intelligence. Following the PRISMA methodology, records were identified, screened, and assessed for eligibility before thirty studies were included in the final synthesis. The review develops a thematic comparison of methods, datasets, and reported limitations, and visualises the distribution of studies by theme and publication year. The synthesis shows that while detection accuracy for individual cybercrime types is now very high, very few studies combine adaptive learning, real-time citizen-facing notification, and plain-language explanation into a single system. Seven specific research gaps are identified, and directions for future work on citizen-oriented, adaptive, and explainable cybercrime early-warning systems are proposed. Keywords: Cybercrime detection; phishing; smishing; social engineering; adaptive learning; explainable artificial intelligence; systematic literature review; citizen cybersecurity

Critical raw material (CRM) exploration increasingly combines Earth Observation, geophysics, geochemistry, mineral prospectivity mapping, probabilistic modelling, and autonomous sensing. However, these capabilities are commonly developed or deployed as separate components, while the explicit coupling of observation, uncertainty-aware geological inference, and subsequent exploration decisions remains comparatively underdeveloped. This paper presents Closed-Loop Mineral Intelligence (CLMI) as a conceptual and methodological framework for organising these capabilities within an iterative Observe–Model–Decide process. The contribution does not propose a new stand-alone learning algorithm or claim an operationally validated exploration system. Instead, it formalises a reference architecture in which heterogeneous observations update probabilistic geological representations, uncertainty informs the prioritisation of subsequent observations, and expert oversight remains part of the decision loop. The framework is examined through an illustrative lithium-bearing pegmatite scenario that specifies the intended information flow, candidate data sources, modelling functions, decision points, and human intervention without reporting empirical performance. A validation roadmap is further defined to make the framework testable in future case studies, including requirements for benchmark baselines, uncertainty calibration, information-gain assessment, exploration-efficiency metrics, computational feasibility, and human–AI interaction. By distinguishing established technological components from the proposed system-level integration, the paper positions CLMI as a research framework and agenda for adaptive, uncertainty-aware mineral exploration rather than as a demonstrated replacement for current professional practice.

Closed-loop reinforcement learning offers a promising approach to integrating generative molecular design with automated chemical synthesis and experimental evaluation. However, translating autonomous chemical optimization into pharmaceutical discovery remains challenging because biological measurements are often delayed, variable, and affected by assay limitations. This critical review and perspective examines current autonomous discovery platforms and evaluates the challenges associated with incorporating physical experimental feedback into molecular optimization. It proposes an uncertainty-aware, multi-objective reward architecture and a four-gate qualification framework covering operational synthesizability, analytical identity and purity, biological assay validity, and governed policy updating. Particular attention is given to distinguishing statistically censored measurements from pharmacologically confounded or invalid observations. The article also introduces supervised autonomy as a practical governance approach in which automated systems perform routine experimental operations while scientific experts retain responsibility for critical decisions. The proposed framework provides a foundation for improving the reliability, interpretability, and practical implementation of experimentally informed molecular discovery. Prospective validation remains necessary to establish its effectiveness.

In response to the increasing reliance on artificial intelligence (AI) in business and college classrooms, an exercise is proposed that reaffirms the fundamental and essential functions reason and creativity perform in personalizing and vitalizing professional communications. Three competing proposals—two generated by AI; one developed without AI assistance—are evaluated in terms of how effectively they answer an assignment from senior management. Alongside highlighting the strengths and limitations of AI’s consensus-based alternatives, the evaluations provide students with a practical demonstration of the substantive contributions human cognition makes to the production of quality communications and to enhancing the reputation of the communicator.

Critical thinking is an essential competency in science education because it enables students to analyze information, evaluate evidence, draw inferences, and make reasoned decisions. Cognitive conflict—arising when students’ prior conceptions encounter information or phenomena inconsistent with their existing understanding—may provide opportunities to reconsider explanations and examine evidence. This review examines (1) how cognitive conflict strategies have been designed and implemented to support critical thinking in science education, (2) how critical thinking has been operationalized and assessed, and (3) opportunities and challenges associated with integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and adaptive learning. The study uses a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) with narrative synthesis. Sixteen articles were mapped for the period October 10, 2016–October 10, 2026. The mapped literature includes studies on cognitive conflict in physics education, instructional media development, critical thinking assessment, conceptual change, and GenAI use. The preliminary synthesis indicates that cognitive conflict has been integrated into inquiry learning, discovery learning, interactive multimedia, e-books, augmented reality, and educational websites. However, only a small subset of the mapped studies directly measured critical thinking, while others focused on conceptual understanding, misconception remediation, scientific literacy, creativity, or product development. The GenAI literature provides contextual insights into personalization and the risk of reduced cognitive engagement, but does not establish the effectiveness of integrating GenAI with cognitive conflict in physics education. The review identifies a need to align cognitive conflict activities with measurable critical thinking indicators and to evaluate GenAI as a scaffold.

documents.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether a commercially available large language model (LLM) can score medical student post-encounter notes from Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) using an existing institutional rubric without task-specific model training and to characterize internal consistency and alignment with faculty scores using absolute agreement and rank-order association metrics. METHOD: The dataset included 433 medical student notes from 7 standardized OSCE cases at the University of Kentucky. In November 2024, an LLM (OpenAI GPT-4o mini, via API) scored each note using a prompt-based workflow (no model fine-tuning) under two approaches: numerical score only ("GPT-NE", 30 iterations per note) and numerical score with rationale ("GPT-E", 4 iterations per note). The authors compared the LLM's performance against historical faculty grades using the same rubric, evaluating the reliability of grading methodologies and inter-modal agreement. RESULTS: The LLM demonstrated high internal consistency for GPT-NE (intraclass correlation (ICC) = 0.94) and moderate-to-high consistency for GPT-E (ICC = 0.76). LLM scores were significantly lower than faculty scores (mean differences on a 1-4 scale: -1.12 GPT-NE, 95% CI -1.17 to -1.08; -0.65 GPT-E, 95% CI -0.69 to -0.61, both P < .001). Spearman rank-order correlations (r = 0.43-0.53) indicate moderate preservation of relative student ranking despite differences in absolute scores. CONCLUSIONS: The LLM demonstrated significant potential for automating OSCE note grading given its internal consistency and similar ranking of learners compared with faculty raters. Automation of grading could yield substantial time savings; however, discrepancies with absolute faculty scores underscore the need for further refinement of rubric alignment and grading methodologies.

documents.abstract: This study, Comparative Biodiversity of Vertebrates in Maharashtra Ecosystems, examines vertebrate diversity, distribution, and ecological roles across Maharashtra’s varied landscapes, including forests, wetlands, rivers, reservoirs, grasslands, coastal zones, and arid regions. Maharashtra is recognised as one of India’s ecological hotspots, supporting a wide range of mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fishes. By comparing vertebrate biodiversity across these ecosystems, the study identifies environmental and human factors that influence species richness and ecological balance. Using scientific literature, biodiversity surveys, government reports, and conservation databases, we mapped vertebrate diversity and the challenges it faces. Our findings indicate that forests and wetlands, due to their complex habitats and abundant water, support the highest vertebrate diversity. In contrast, Maharashtra’s semi-arid and urban areas support fewer species, with habitat loss and ongoing human activity reducing biodiversity. The study identifies key threats, including deforestation, pollution, urban expansion, climate change, roadkill, agricultural growth, mining, and increasing human-wildlife conflict. Freshwater and coastal habitats are particularly vulnerable to pollution and unregulated development, while forests face growing fragmentation. The research emphasises the importance of protected areas, wildlife corridors, wetland conservation, habitat restoration, and continuous ecological monitoring. Conservation strategies should be tailored to each ecosystem's specific needs. The study ultimately calls for an integrated, ecosystem-based approach that combines scientific research, community involvement, effective policy, and sustainable management to protect Maharashtra’s vertebrate diversity.

Artificial intelligence (AI) and CRISPR-based genome editing offer complementary approaches to investigating genetic variation and developing targeted interventions in precision medicine. This narrative review examines the principles underlying AI-assisted genomic analysis and programmable genome editing, with particular attention to their potential integration in disease research and therapeutic development. Machine learning and deep learning models can analyse genomic and other molecular datasets, assist in identifying disease-associated variants, and support the prioritisation of candidate therapeutic targets. In CRISPR research, computational methods can inform guide RNA selection, estimate editing efficiency and potential off-target activity, and assist in interpreting functional screening results. Combining these approaches may improve the selection of experimental targets and strengthen investigation of biological mechanisms relevant to inherited disorders, cancer and other complex conditions. The review also discusses AI-assisted clinical decision support, pharmacogenomics, and applications of genome editing in molecular research. However, the reliability of integrated approaches remains dependent on representative training data, transparent computational methods, appropriate experimental validation and safe delivery of editing components. Unintended genomic alterations, variable editing outcomes, model bias, data privacy concerns, ethical issues and regulatory requirements continue to constrain clinical translation. Further progress will require reproducible research, long-term safety assessment and interdisciplinary collaboration. Overall, AI-guided CRISPR research may contribute to the development of more individualised therapeutic strategies, but its clinical value must be established through rigorous validation and responsible implementation.

documents.abstract: The use of modern technologies is revolutionizing all spheres of life, including industry, on which the economic development and stability of the country and the population in general depend. The various modern intelligent systems used in warehouses, depots, and large factories assist the production process, management, and optimization of the purchase and sale of stock. Various artificial intelligence and blockchain techniques have transformed traditional systems into digital, intelligent, decentralized and secure platforms, but have also facilitated physical processes through the use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and other intelligent agents, which directly impact productivity and cost-efficiency in the supply chain. The use of hybrid architectures, which will combine the advantages of contemporary technologies, with the aim of creating a secure, transparent ecosystem, where privacy, traceability, and above all a longer-term strategy for efficient stock management will be created, is of particular importance in the supply chain. Furthermore, the use of smart contracts, which in addition to automating processes on the blockchain network, also reduces human intervention and possible delays, and at the same time protects the supply chain from possible manipulations that could be threatened by malicious persons. Despite the fact that the integration of contemporary technologies leads to the improvement and facilitation of stock management processes, many challenges of practical implementation, scalability, and system interoperability such as the lack of standardization, privacy and ethical issues remain among the many challenges facing modern intelligent systems. Through this paper, we will first explain the importance of integrating contemporary technologies, in particular blockchain technology and artificial intelligence, into the inventory management process, and then propose a conceptual model for integrating these technologies into existing intelligent systems, with the aim of creating a more secure, transparent and reliable supply chain. We will also present an intelligent stock management system, which we have tested and is functional, with the aim of integrating functionalities from contemporary technologies into it in the future, to offer the highest quality and safest services.

documents.abstract: Conformal prediction offers distribution-free coverage guarantees for machine-learning emulators of climate extremes, but the guarantee is only as good as the exchangeability assumption that underwrites it. Using NASA POWER monthly reanalysis for Kampala, Uganda (0.35°N, 32.58°E) over 2000–2023 (312 observations, mean 22.443 °C, linear trend −0.1564 °C per decade), the study specifies a graph construction, a split-conformal calibration protocol, and a coverage-degradation bound expressed as a function of a scenario-shift divergence. The analysis derives a finite-sample coverage gap under covariate shift, proposes a weighted conformal score that restores approximate validity, and identifies the conditions under which GNN emulators of regional extremes can be certified for out-of-distribution emissions scenarios. The contribution is a formal account of when conformal coverage survives scenario shift and a diagnostic that practitioners can compute before deploying an emulator.

documents.abstract: A smartphone holds a person's messages, photographs, bank apps and location. A new kind of app is arriving on it: the AI agent that acts for the user, reading the screen, opening other apps and carrying out tasks. To work, such an agent needs permissions, and an agent that is hijacked, impersonated or simply drifts from its task can misuse them. Today's protections are a permission gate that lists what an agent may call, and live on-device checks that warn the user or disable an app once its behaviour is judged malicious. This concept note proposes a live layer between them. For each AI agent, a lag-1 autocorrelation warning number is calculated at run time from the agent's own behaviour stream, mainly the run of requests that fall outside the user's task and its use of sensitive permissions. The computer then decides a graded shunting action: confirmation is asked, the agent's permissions are lowered, or the agent is hand-tied, while the phone and every other app keep running. This is a concept to be tested on real phone traffic, not a result. Patent pending.

Seasonal forecast advisories are promoted as a climate service that raises crop yields, yet extension agencies typically target farmers who already differ from non-adopters in ways that also affect yield. the present analysis formalises the resulting adoption-selection bias and evaluates a doubly robust estimator for counterfactual yield attribution under a declared data-generating process. The design is a replication-based evaluation: 600 data sets of N = 500 were drawn from a process with intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35 and error SD 4.2, and the ordinary least squares estimator was characterised across replications. The estimated bias was -0.04629 for the intercept and 0.00086 for the exposure coefficient; the root mean squared errors were 0.95661 and 0.01664 respectively, and empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The results indicate that under correct specification the estimator recovers the exposure effect with negligible bias and conservative coverage, but that the intercept is the fragile quantity when group composition is unbalanced. Doubly robust attribution is defensible for advisory evaluation only when the selection model is reported alongside the outcome model, and it derives the conditions under which extension targeting can be interpreted as a counterfactual yield effect rather than a description of adopters.

Urban unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) fleets require coordinated optimization of communication, mobility, and energy management. This study evaluates conventional and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled cross-layer protocol suites in a common five-hour simulation of 7,500 UAVs, 240 base stations, and 40 vertiports across 144 km². They include AODV-based conventional routing, reinforcement learning-based UAV-AI-EDRL, federated ANN-PID-based UAV-AI-FHAP, reduced learning baselines, and a composite. Methodological contributions comprise a mission-constrained cross-layer objective, CMA-ES calibration benchmarks, physics-grounded training, paired evaluation over six environmental realizations, and packet-level NS-3 checks. In fleet-scale runs, proactive routing reduced mean end-to-end delay from 66.0 to 25.3 ms (61.6%), an advantage NS-3 reproduced at every transmit power only with pre-resolved link-layer addresses. UAV-AI-EDRL reduced power by 8.7% and near-miss events by 18.1% on the principal training seed, although safety gains varied across seeds. UAV-AI-FHAP reduced power by 4.6% and near-miss events by 30.9%, but completed 15.9% fewer missions because a charging threshold calibrated on a reduced-area oracle interrupted long delivery legs; geometry-preserving recalibration reduced the deficit to 2.2%, and a leg-aware charging rule produced a 13.9% gain (2.3% if the conventional suite also uses it). Ablations with equivalence tests attributed the gains to proactive forwarding, throttling, spread control, and reactive avoidance, finding no measurable suite-level benefit from DQN, PPO, path planning, ANN-PID, or federated aggregation; suites without learned power control preserved superior raw radio metrics. These findings, limited to the simulated conditions, shifts, and fleet sizes, reveal trade-offs among latency, energy, safety, and mission completion, emphasizing operationally weighted selection and field validation.

Semiconductor manufacturing underpins digital economies, artificial intelligence, telecommunications, automotive systems and national technological security. This review examines the global semiconductor value chain, compares the strengths and constraints of major producing economies, and evaluates technological and industrial prospects for 2026–2035. It highlights advanced logic, memory, chiplets, compound semiconductors, supply-chain diversification and opportunities for Vietnam. The analysis distinguishes current industrial capabilities from future policy targets and emphasizes the importance of human resources, infrastructure and international cooperation.

This book develops a unified governance framework for systems that retrieve, generate, infer, remember and act on information from large language models and retrieval augmented pipelines to autonomous multi agent systems. Eleven chapters and eight appendices integrate three disciplinary lenses-technology, law and economics-across the full lifecycle: data quality, lineage and provenance; global data protection law and intellectual property; the economics of data governance; digital trust, cybersecurity and zero-trust architecture; ethics and responsible AI; governing generative AI pipelines; governing agentic AI and multi-agent systems; data governance in elections and the public sphere; AI regulation across six jurisdictions; and the design of a governance control plane for 2030. Each chapter is anchored in Indian law and institutions while maintaining a comparative, cross jurisdictional perspective.

documents.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have transformed knowledge discovery, but their use in sensitive domains is limited by privacy concerns and risks of data leakage. Moreover, LLMs may hallucinate when queried about information outside their training data, undermining their reliability for scientific, clinical, or policy-related tasks. We present MyGPT, a fully open-source, privacy-preserving retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) platform that uses open-source LLMs and operates locally or within secure institutional environments. MyGPT empowers users to query user-defined libraries such as biomedical literature, confidential clinical documents, and multilingual global health policies, while ensuring that sensitive data never leaves the secure environment. We introduce confidence metrics, including “relevance scores” and “hallucination index,” and provide explicit source citation from the library within a single interface to assess contextual support for generated answers. MyGPT offers a cost-effective, modular, open-source alternative to commercial LLM services and democratizes knowledge-seeking across multiple domains, including use at remote facilities without internet access.

documents.abstract: As AI coding agents become more autonomous, developers increasingly direct, coordinate, and check their work. Yet little is known about these practices in everyday professional development. We shadowed 11 professional developers across approximately 15 hours of work, coded their activities and task transitions, analyzed 255 submitted prompts, and conducted 4.6 hours of follow-up interviews. Developers spent an average of 33.4% of observed time formulating prompts or checking AI responses, with task-switching rates ranging from 0 to 101.6 switches per hour. Beyond producing artifacts, prompts supported understanding, requirements clarification, agent configuration, and coordination. We identified three recurring patterns: \textit{Supervisor}, involving direct artifact inspection; \textit{Delegator}, involving dialogue-based coordination and delegated implementation and checking; and \textit{Learner}, involving agents primarily to build understanding. Developers sought technical information from agents and organizational context, authority, and alignment from colleagues. Our findings suggest future studies of how developers manage attention across concurrent agent tasks and tools that support verification, coordination, and learning.

Introduction: Collaboration and cooperation among universities are among the ways to promote shared global well-being. To achieve this, universities must take a proactive role in managing inter-institutional agreements so that they contribute to educational quality Objective: To demonstrate the contribution of an intelligent assessment, mediated by artificial intelligence and grounded in a systemic-historical-cultural approach, to the management of inter-institutional agreements in order to enhance the quality of university education. Method: This research followed a mixed-methods approach that was descriptive and propositional in nature, with a qualitative focus. Theoretical methods were used to construct the conceptual and epistemological framework of the proposal, including synthetic-analytic, inductive-deductive, and theoretical modeling approaches. Additionally, a literature review was conducted. Journals from Scopus, Web of Science, SciELO, Redalyc, Dialnet, DOAJ, institutional repositories, and specialized sources on Artificial Intelligence and education were consulted, covering the time period 2000–2025. The literature review process was organized into three stages: initial exploration, in-depth analysis, and systematization and integration. Results: The analysis conducted made it possible to characterize the management of agreements, the limitations of traditional assessment, the role, applications, and ethical principles of Artificial Intelligence as a mediator in such management, and a proposal for its three phases to enhance the quality of higher education. Conclusions: It is concluded that intelligent assessment contributes to educational quality through five mechanisms: strategic alignment, data-driven management, predictive capacity, ethical and social strengthening, and institutional learning. The proposal represents a significant step forward in transforming the management of agreements into a driver of quality and social change.

Artificial intelligence (AI) now decides who receives police protection and who gets government benefits and who gets employment or credit approval and who gets their online content promoted or deleted. The academic research and legal regulations that follow treat the resulting privacy violations and the breaks of equality and the restrictions on free speech as different issues. The paper presents three interrelated elements which demonstrate their relationship through three specific aspects: surveillance and profiling drive people to stop talking then automated content control systems create unfair distribution of when users speak and finally data practices which privacy legislation aims to control lead to unfair scoring outcomes. The study employs doctrinal and comparative approaches to examine three questions: (1) Do Articles 14, 19(1)(a) and 21 of the Indian Constitution provide sufficient protection against AI-related harms (2) What are the strengths and weaknesses of European Union and United States regulations governing AI systems used by public and private organizations (3) What protective measures should India implement. The Indian constitutional doctrine demonstrates strong power but the Indian legal system fails to provide sufficient support for automated decision-making and State exemptions and private-sector discrimination and remedies. The system establishes a comprehensive framework that consists of four hierarchical levels which include constitutional and legislative and institutional and remedial components. The law is stated as at 19 October 2026.

documents.abstract: This paper examines the interrelation between the development of the digital economy and the enhancement of regional competitiveness, focusing on the use of remote sensing and artificial intelligence (AI) to assess the socio-economic condition of regions, and poverty levels in particular. By integrating nighttime lights (NTL) imagery with geographic information system (GIS) technologies and machine learning, the study proposes data-driven analytical tools that complement demographic and economic statistics and support evidence-based regional policy.

documents.abstract: The Industrial Revolution 4.0 has significantly transformed various aspects of human life, particularly in education and employment, through the integration of digital technology, artificial intelligence, big data, and the Internet of Things. These rapid changes demand new competencies such as digital literacy, critical thinking, adaptability, and career flexibility. In response to these challenges, digital-based career counseling has emerged as a strategic innovation to support students’ career development and readiness for the modern workplace. This study employs a literature review approach by analyzing recent national and international scientific publications indexed in Sinta, Scopus, and Google Scholar within the last five years. The analysis focuses on key themes including theoretical foundations, implementation models, benefits, and challenges of digital career counseling. The findings indicate that integrating classical career theories, such as Holland’s RIASEC personality typology and Super’s life-span, life-space theory, with digital platforms enhances accessibility, efficiency, and personalization of counseling services. Digital tools such as video conferencing, learning management systems, online assessments, and social media platforms contribute to improving career adaptability, career optimism, and employability skills among students. However, challenges remain in terms of counselors’ digital competence, ethical considerations, data security, and maintaining emotional connection in virtual interactions. Therefore, successful implementation of digital-based career counseling requires collaboration among government institutions, educational organizations, and technology developers to ensure effective, ethical, and student-centered services in the era of the Industrial Revolution 4.0.

The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the management and operational processes of the hospitality industry. Boutique hotels, characterized by relatively small room capacity, personalized services, distinctive design, and strong dependence on guest experience, require flexible and data-driven approaches to improving operational and economic efficiency. This article examines the directions for improving the efficiency of boutique hotels through artificial intelligence-based modeling. Particular attention is given to AI applications in demand forecasting, dynamic pricing, occupancy optimization, guest personalization, workforce planning, energy management, digital marketing, and operational decision-making. The study proposes an integrated AI-based efficiency model that combines historical booking data, room prices, occupancy rates, customer reviews, seasonal factors, events, weather conditions, and online market information. The article also considers machine learning, neural networks, time-series forecasting, ensemble models, and explainable artificial intelligence as tools for supporting managerial decisions. Recent research demonstrates that AI-based forecasting can improve the accuracy of hotel demand prediction, while AI-driven personalization can support revenue stability and guest engagement. However, effective implementation requires high-quality data, appropriate technological infrastructure, employee competencies, data protection, and human supervision. The study concludes that AI-based modeling should be considered not as a replacement for hotel managers but as a decision-support mechanism that can improve resource allocation, pricing decisions, service personalization, and overall economic efficiency.
